It is conservative since\nall\n$\\textnormal{coind}^{G_i}_{HN_i/N_i}:\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{HN_i/N_i} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i}$\nare, and the family of categorical fixed point functors\n$(-)^{H\\cap N_i}: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{H} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{HN_i/N_i}$\nindexed by $i \\in I$ is jointly conservative. The description of the\nalgebra object in the finite index case is the same as in\n[1](#cons:colimitoforbits){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cons:colimitoforbits\"}. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *The previous lemma is a striking difference to the case\nwhere $G$ is a compact Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed\nsubgroup, here $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H$ in general fails to be\nconservative [@mnn17 Warning p.1034]. In the compact Lie case the\nrestriction $\\textnormal{res}^G_H$ always has a left adjoint\n$\\textnormal{ind}^G_H$ that is related to $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H$ via a\nWirthmüller isomorphism. On the contrary, in the profinite case\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_H$ for $H$ again an arbitrary closed subgroup might\nnot have a left adjoint, although its right adjoint\n$\\textnormal{coind}^G_H$ always preserves colimits, cf.\n[1](#rem:changeofgroupspectralmackey){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:changeofgroupspectralmackey\"}. This goes in line with the\nfact that tensoring with $\\textnormal{coind}^{G}_H(R_{H})$, or\nequivalently applying $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H\\textnormal{res}^G_H$,\nmight not preserve limits - we will see below that there is generally no\nreason to expect that $\\textnormal{coind}^{G}_H(R_{H})$ is compact (and\nhence neither dualisable).*\n:::\n\nWhen we work with an arbitrary closed subgroup $H \\leq G$, the only\ncaveat of the previous lemma is that $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H(R_H)$ is\nnot a very explicit description of the algebra object we are working\nwith. For $H=1$ we will give a description of the functor\n$\\textnormal{coind}^G_1\\textnormal{res}^G_1$ as tensoring with the\nalgebra object $A_R$ from\n[1](#cons:colimitoforbits){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cons:colimitoforbits\"}. We first prove a general statement\nabout filtered colimits of monadic adjunctions.\\\nRecall from [@mnn17 Construction 5.23] (or from\n[1](#rec:modules){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"rec:modules\"})\nthat if we have an adjunction\n$(L,R): \\mathcal{M}\\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{N}$ of presentably\nsymmetric monoidal $\\infty$-categories where $L$ is symmetric monoidal,\nthen the right adjoint applied to the unit\n$R(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}})$ has a commutative algebra structure and\nthere is an induced adjunction\n$$(\\bar{L},\\bar{R}): \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}})}(\\mathcal{M}) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{N}$$\nfor which the left adjoint $\\bar{L}$ factors as\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}})}(\\mathcal{M}) \\stackrel{L}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{LR(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}})}(\\mathcal{N}) \\stackrel{\\varepsilon_!}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{N}$,\nwhere\n$\\varepsilon: LR(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}}) \\to \\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nis the counit map. We will say that the adjunction $(L,R)$ is *monadic*\nif the induced adjunction $(\\bar{L},\\bar{R})$ is an equivalence.\n\n::: {#lem:filteredcolimitofmonadicadjunctions .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *Let $\\mathcal{C}$ be a filtered $\\infty$-category that has\nan initial object $X_0$ and let\n$\\mathcal{E}: \\mathcal{C}\\to \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}})$\nbe a functor. Write $f_{X} = \\mathcal{E}(X_0 \\to X)$ and $g_X$ for its\nright adjoint. Assume that for every $X \\in \\mathcal{C}$ the adjunction\n$$(f_{X},g_{X}): \\mathcal{E}(X_0) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{E}(X)$$ is\nmonadic. Set\n$\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty} = \\textnormal{colim}_{\\mathcal{C}} \\; \\mathcal{E}$,\nwhere the colimit is taken in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}})$. Then the\ninduced adjunction\n$$(f_{{\\infty}},g_{\\infty}): \\mathcal{E}(X_0) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}$$\nis monadic. In particular, there is an equivalence\n$\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{g_{\\infty}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}})}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$,\nand the commutative algebra object\n$g_{\\infty}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}})$ is equivalent to the\nfiltered colimit of the $g_{X}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}(X)})$ in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* This is an application of [@agv22 Lemma 3.5.6] which computes\nfiltered colimits of module categories with extensions of scalars\nbetween them.\\\nWe write $A_X$ for\n$g_{X}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}(X)}) \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$.\nThe assignment $X \\mapsto A_X$ determines a filtered diagram\n$\\epsilon: \\mathcal{C}\\to \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$, and we\nwrite $A_{\\infty}$ for its colimit. Then by [@lur17 Theorem 4.8.5.11]\nthe functor $\\mathcal{E}$ identifies with the composition\n$$\\mathcal{C}\\stackrel{\\epsilon}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0)) \\stackrel{\\widehat{\\Theta}_*}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}})_{\\mathcal{E}(X_0)/} \\stackrel{\\textnormal{fgt}}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}), \\; X \\mapsto \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{A_X}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0)),$$\nwhere $\\widehat{\\Theta}_*$ is as in [@lur17 Notation 4.8.5.10]. Applying\n[@agv22 Lemma 3.5.6] to the constant functor\n$X \\mapsto \\mathcal{E}(X_0)$ and the diagram of algebra objects\n$\\epsilon$ gives an equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{A_{\\infty}}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$$\nunder which the left adjoint\n$f_{\\infty}: \\mathcal{E}(X_0) \\to \\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}$ identifies with\nthe free module functor $A_{\\infty} \\otimes (-)$. In particular, by\napplying its right adjoint $g_{\\infty}$ to the unit of\n$\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}$ we see that\n$g_{\\infty}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}}) \\simeq A_{\\infty}$ in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty})$. This concludes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:monads .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *Since in the previous lemma the monads $g_Xf_X$ and\n$g_{\\infty}f_{\\infty}$ in $\\textnormal{End}(\\mathcal{E}(X_0))$ are\ndetermined by the algebra objects $g_{X}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}(X)})$\nand $g_{\\infty}(\\mathbbm{1}_{\\mathcal{E}_{\\infty}})$ they tensor with,\nthe lemma implies that the monad $g_{\\infty}f_{\\infty}$ is the colimit\nof the monads $g_Xf_X$ taken in endofunctors of $\\mathcal{E}(X_0)$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:spectraascolimit .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *There is a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i}) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nwhere the colimit is taken in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}_{\\textnormal{st}})$\nalong the restrictions $\\textnormal{res}^{N_j}_{N_i}$ for\n$N_i \\subseteq N_j$.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Consider the filtered diagram $$\\begin{align*}\n&\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_{\\bullet}}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_\\bullet}): I^\\textnormal{op}\\to \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}_{\\textnormal{st}}), \\; i \\mapsto \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i}), \\\\\n&(N_i \\subseteq N_j) \\mapsto (\\textnormal{res}_{N_i}^{N_j}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_j}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_j}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})).\n\\end{align*}$$ Restricting from each $N_i$ to the trivial subgroup\ninduces a symmetric monoidal left adjoint\n$\\varphi: \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.\nFor $X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$, its\ninflation $\\textnormal{infl}^{N_i}_1(X)$ to\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})$ (for any\n$i$) has restriction\n$\\textnormal{res}^{N_i}_1\\textnormal{infl}^{N_i}_1(X) \\simeq X$, hence\n$\\varphi$ is essentially surjective. Since the restrictions in the\ncolimit diagram preserve compact objects their colimit is compactly\ngenerated, and by [@lur09 Proposition 5.3.5.11] it suffices to show that\n$\\varphi$ is fully faithful when restricted to compacts.\\\nThe compact part of\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})$\nis $\\mathcal{C}\\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})$,\nwhere the filtered colimit is computed in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Cat}}_{\\infty}$. For two objects\n$\\bar{X}, \\bar{Y} \\in \\mathcal{C}$ we can assume without restriction\nthat they are of the form $\\varphi_k(X)$ and $\\varphi_k(Y)$\nrespectively, where $X$ and $Y$ are compact objects of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_k}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_k})$ for the\nsame index $k$ and $\\varphi_k$ is the structure map\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_k}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_k}) \\to \\mathcal{C}$.\nWe can furthermore reduce to the case where the objects $X$ and $Y$ are\ncompact generators, i.e. of the form\n$\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ N_k/H \\otimes R_{N_k}$ and\n$\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ N_k/H' \\otimes R_{N_k}$ for two open subgroups\n$H,H' \\leq N_k$. We hence consider the map $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:varphimappingspaces}\n\\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{C}}(\\bar{X},\\bar{Y}) \\stackrel{\\varphi}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}(\\varphi(\\bar{X}),\\varphi(\\bar{Y}))\n\\end{equation}$$ induced by $\\varphi$ on mapping spaces. Note that the\nfunctor $(I^\\textnormal{op})_{k/} \\to I^\\textnormal{op}$ is cofinal\n[@lur09 Example 5.4.5.9, Lemma 5.4.5.12], hence by [@lur09 Proposition\n4.1.1.8] the left-hand side of\n[\\[eq:varphimappingspaces\\]](#eq:varphimappingspaces){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:varphimappingspaces\"} identifies with\n$$\\textnormal{colim}_{i \\geq k} \\; \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ \\textnormal{res}^{N_k}_{N_i}(N_j/H) \\otimes R_{N_i},\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ \\textnormal{res}^{N_k}_{N_i}(N_j/H') \\otimes R_{N_i}),$$\nwhere we understand $i \\geq k$ as $N_i \\subseteq N_k$. Now there is a\n$k' \\geq k$ such that for all $i \\geq k'$ the normal subgroup $N_i$ is\ncontained in both $H$ and $H'$ and hence acts trivially on $N_k/H$ and\n$N_k/H'$. Using the same cofinality argument as before, we can thus\nfurther reduce to showing that the map $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:varphimappingspacesreduced}\n\\textnormal{colim}_{i} \\; \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})}(R_{N_i},R_{N_i}) \\stackrel{\\varphi}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}(R,R)\n\\end{equation}$$ is an equivalence. Since each\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_i}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_i})$\nis itself a colimit along inflation, the left-hand side of\n[\\[eq:varphimappingspacesreduced\\]](#eq:varphimappingspacesreduced){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:varphimappingspacesreduced\"}, where we write\n$N_{ij} \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=N_iN_j/N_j$, identifies with $$\\begin{align}\n&\\underset{i, \\, \\textnormal{res}}{\\textnormal{colim}} \\; \\; \\underset{j, \\, \\textnormal{infl}}{\\textnormal{colim}} \\; \\; \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_{ij}}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_{ij}})}(R_{N_{ij}},R_{N_{ij}}) \\notag \\\\\n\\simeq \\; &\\underset{j, \\, \\textnormal{infl}}{\\textnormal{colim}} \\; \\; \\underset{i, \\, \\textnormal{res}}{\\textnormal{colim}} \\; \\; \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{N_{ij}}}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{N_{ij}})}(R_{N_{ij}},R_{N_{ij}}). \\label{eq:finalmappingspace}\n\\end{align}$$ But for each $j$, there is an $i'$ such that\n$N_i \\subseteq N_j$ for all $i \\geq i'$, and in this case\n$N_{ij}=N_iN_j/N_j$ is trivial. Using cofinality once more, this shows\nthat\n[\\[eq:finalmappingspace\\]](#eq:finalmappingspace){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:finalmappingspace\"} is given by\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}^{\\omega}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}(R,R)$,\nand the map\n[\\[eq:varphimappingspacesreduced\\]](#eq:varphimappingspacesreduced){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:varphimappingspacesreduced\"} is an equivalence, as\ndesired. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#cor:identifycolimitoforbits .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *There is an equivalence\n$\\textnormal{coind}^G_1(R) \\simeq A_R$ in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G))$.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Apply\n[1](#lem:filteredcolimitofmonadicadjunctions){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:filteredcolimitofmonadicadjunctions\"} to the diagram of\n[1](#lem:spectraascolimit){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:spectraascolimit\"}, using\n[1](#lem:resasbasechangeprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:resasbasechangeprofinite\"}. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#cor:endofunctors .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *There are equivalences of endofunctors of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\n$$(A_R \\otimes_{R_G} -) \\simeq \\textnormal{coind}^G_1\\textnormal{res}^G_1 \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textnormal{coind}^G_{N_i}\\textnormal{res}^G_{N_i}.$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* This follows from\n[1](#lem:resasbasechangeprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:resasbasechangeprofinite\"},\n[1](#cor:identifycolimitoforbits){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:identifycolimitoforbits\"} and\n[1](#rem:monads){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"rem:monads\"}. ◻\n:::\n\n::: ex\n**Example 1**. *Using adjunction and\n[1](#cor:identifycolimitoforbits){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:identifycolimitoforbits\"} we obtain an equivalence\n$$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}}(\\mathbb{S},\\mathbb{S}) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ G/N_i,\\mathbb{S}_G),$$\nwhich on $\\pi_0$ recovers the fact that the filtered colimit of the\ngroup completions of the monoids of finite $N_i$-sets under disjoint\nunion $\\pi_0^{N_i}(\\mathbb{S}_G) \\cong \\mathbb{A}_{\\mathbb{Z}}(G/N_i)$\nis $\\mathbb{Z}$.*\n:::\n\nLet us fix some terminology for t-structures we will use throughout this\npaper.\n\n::: {#def:hypercompletetstructure .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *Let $\\mathcal{C}$ be a stable $\\infty$-category with\na t-structure $(\\mathcal{C}_{\\geq 0},\\mathcal{C}_{\\leq 0})$ and denote\nby $\\pi_n(-): \\mathcal{C}\\to \\mathcal{C}^{\\heartsuit}$ its integer\nindexed homotopy object functors. We say that an object\n$X \\in \\mathcal{C}$ is*\n\n1.  **acyclic* if $\\pi_n(X) = 0$ for all $n \\in \\mathbb{Z}$,*\n\n2.  **hypercomplete* if\n    $\\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{C}}(Y,X) \\simeq \\ast$ for all acyclic\n    $Y \\in \\mathcal{C}$.*\n\n*We call $\\mathcal{C}$ *hypercomplete* if all of its objects are\nhypercomplete.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *That $\\mathcal{C}$ is hypercomplete is equivalent to all\nacyclic objects being zero. If the t-structure on $\\mathcal{C}$ is right\ncomplete then hypercompleteness is equivalent to the t-structure being\nleft separated, i.e.\n$\\bigcap_{n \\in \\mathbb{Z}} \\mathcal{C}_{\\geq n} = 0$. Again assuming\nright completeness, hypercompleteness is implied by Postnikov\ncompleteness, which asserts that for every object $X$ the canonical map\n$X \\to \\lim_{n\\geq 0} \\tau_{\\leq n} X$ is an equivalence. The latter is\nprecisely the statement that the canonical map\n$\\mathcal{C}\\to \\textnormal{lim}_{n \\geq 0} \\; \\mathcal{C}_{\\leq n}$ is\nfully faithful. This map being an equivalence is the condition that the\nt-structure on $\\mathcal{C}$ is left complete.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *It is clear from the definition that the full subcategory\nof hypercomplete objects $\\mathcal{C}^h \\subseteq \\mathcal{C}$ is closed\nunder limits. If $\\mathcal{C}$ is additionally assumed to be presentable\nand its t-structure is compatible with filtered colimits then the\ninclusion $\\mathcal{C}^h \\hookrightarrow C$ has an accessible left\nadjoint we denote by $L^h: \\mathcal{C}\\to \\mathcal{C}^h$ [@cm21\nProposition 2.14], [@lur18 Proposition C.1.4.1]. Note that\n$\\mathcal{C}^h$ inherits a t-structure that makes the functor $L^h$\nt-exact. If $\\mathcal{C}$ is furthermore presentably symmetric monoidal\nand this symmetric monoidal structure is compatible with the t-structure\n(i.e., the connective part is a symmetric monoidal subcategory), then\n[@cm21 Lemma 2.22] gives a unique symmetric monoidal structure on\n$\\mathcal{C}^h$ that makes the hypercompletion functor symmetric\nmonoidal.*\n:::\n\nRecall that for a finite group Borel complete spectra were defined as\nthe right orthogonal of nonequivariantly contractible spectra. We now\ngive characterisations for the latter notion in the profinite group\ncase. One of them uses the t-structure from\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"}, which in contrast\nto the t-structure on $G$-spectra is only right but generally not left\ncomplete. In particular, there can be nonzero acyclic objects.\n\n::: {#prop:noneqcontractibleprofinite .prop}\n**Proposition 1**. *For an $R_G$-module $X$, the following are\nequivalent:*\n\n1.  *$X$ is nonequivariantly contractible, i.e.\n    $\\textnormal{res}^G_1(X) \\simeq 0$ in\n    $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.*\n\n2.  *$\\textnormal{res}^G_1U_{R_G}(X) \\simeq U_R\\textnormal{res}^G_1(X)$\n    is contractible in $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.*\n\n3.  *$X \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$ in\n    $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$.*\n\n4.  *$U_R(X \\otimes_{R_G} A_R) \\simeq U_R(X) \\otimes A_{\\mathbb{S}}$ is\n    contractible in $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.*\n\n5.  *The levelwise completion $L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X)$ is acyclic, that\n    is $\\pi_n(L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X))=0$ for all $n \\in \\mathbb{Z}$,\n    where the $\\pi_n(-)$ are the t-structure homotopy modules of\n    [1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref\"\n    reference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"}.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* That (1) and (2) are equivalent is clear from the\nconservativity of the forgetful functor and\n[1](#rec:modules){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"rec:modules\"},\nsimilarly that (3) and (4) are equivalent follows from the\nconservativity of the forgetful functor and the projection formula for\nthe free-forgetful adjunction. The equivalence of assertions (1) and (3)\nfollows from the conservativity of $\\textnormal{coind}^G_1$ (see\n[1](#lem:resasbasechangeprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:resasbasechangeprofinite\"}) and\n[1](#cor:endofunctors){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:endofunctors\"}.\\\nWe now show that (3) and (5) are equivalent. Let $X$ be an $R_G$-module.\nBy [@lur09 Lemma 6.3.3.6] we have\n$X \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(X^{N_i})$,\nso\n$$L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, L_{\\textnormal{lw}}\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(X^{N_i}) \\stackrel{\\ref{diag:levelwisecompletion}}{\\simeq} \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}\\theta_i^*(X^{N_i}) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}\\sigma_i^*(X),$$\nwhere $\\theta_i: BG_i \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G_i)^{\\textnormal{op}}$\npicks out the orbit $G_i/1$ and\n$\\sigma_i: BG_i \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}}$ picks\nout the orbit $G/N_i$, using that each of the triangles $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    & {\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}}} \\\\\n    {BG_i} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G_i)^{\\textnormal{op}}}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\sigma_i}\", from=2-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\theta_i}\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\overline{\\textnormal{infl}}^G_{G_i}}\"', from=2-2, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ commutes. (Recall from\n[1](#rem:changeofgroupspectralmackey){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:changeofgroupspectralmackey\"} that categorical fixed\npoints precompose with the vertical functor\n$\\overline{\\textnormal{infl}}^G_{G_i}$ of span categories.) Since the\nt-structure from\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"} is compatible with\nfiltered colimits it follows for its homotopy modules $$\\begin{align*}\n\\pi_n(L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X)) &\\cong \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\pi_n(h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}\\sigma_i^*(X)) \\cong \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, (h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i})^{\\heartsuit} (\\pi_n(\\sigma_i^*(X))) \\\\\n&\\cong \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, (h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i})^{\\heartsuit} \\pi_n^{N_i}(X) \\cong \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\pi_n^{N_i}(X).\n\\end{align*}$$ Here $(h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i})^{\\heartsuit}$ denotes\nthe restriction of $h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}$ to hearts, it is given\nby the ordinary inflation from $(G_i;\\pi_0(R))$-modules to discrete\n$(G;\\pi_0(R))$-modules. We use that $h\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}$ is\nt-exact and hence commutes with homotopy objects. In the last step each\n$\\pi_n^{N_i}(X)$ is viewed as a discrete $(G;\\pi_0(R))$-module.\\\nOn the other hand\n$X \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/N_i \\otimes R, X)$,\nand this $R_G$-module is contractible if and only if its underlying\n$G$-spectrum is, for which contractibility is equivalent to the\nvanishing of all homotopy Mackey functors. For the $n^{\\textnormal{th}}$\none, using that the forgetful functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$\ncommutes with colimits, the $N_j$-sections are given by $$\\begin{align}\n\\pi^{N_j}_n(&\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/N_i, X)) \\notag \\\\\n\\cong \\;&\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textnormal{Hom}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty +n}_+G/N_j, \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/N_i, X)) \\notag \\\\\n\\cong \\;&\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textnormal{Hom}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty +n}_+G/N_j \\times G/N_i, X) \\notag \\\\\n\\cong \\;&\\textnormal{colim}_i \\bigoplus_{[N_j\\backslash G /N_i]} \\pi_n^{N_i\\cap N_j}(X).\n\\label{eq:mackeyintersection}\n\\end{align}$$ Assume the vanishing of $\\pi_n(L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X))$,\nso for all $x\\in \\pi_n^{N_i}(X)$ there is an $N_l \\subseteq N_i$ such\nthat $x$ vanishes in $\\pi_n^{N_l}(X)$. Fix $j$. If $y$ is an element of\n$\\bigoplus_{k \\in [N_j\\backslash G /N_i]} \\; \\pi_n^{N_i\\cap N_j}(X)$\nwith (finitely many) components $y_k \\in \\pi_n^{N_i \\cap N_j}(X)$, then\nthere are $N_{k} \\subseteq N_i\\cap N_j$ such that $y_k$ vanishes in\n$\\pi_n^{N_{k}}(X)$, and hence $y$ vanishes when passing to the sections\nfor the group\n$\\bigcap_k N_{k} = (\\bigcap_k N_{k}) \\cap N_j \\subseteq N_i \\cap N_j$.\\\nConversely, assume that\n[\\[eq:mackeyintersection\\]](#eq:mackeyintersection){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:mackeyintersection\"} vanishes for all $N_j$, then in\nparticular it vanishes for $N_j=G$. Then\n[\\[eq:mackeyintersection\\]](#eq:mackeyintersection){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:mackeyintersection\"} reads\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\pi_n^{N_i}(X)$, which is precisely\n$\\pi_n(L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(X))$. Using this argument for all $n$ shows\nthat (3) and (5) are equivalent, concluding the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *If\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ is compact,\nthen it is inflated from some $G_i$, i.e.\n$X \\simeq \\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(X')$. Then\n$X \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$ is equivalent to\n$\\textnormal{res}^{G_i}_1(X') \\simeq 0$. However, if we write a general\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ as a\nfiltered colimit of compacts $X_j$, then $X \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$\nneed not imply $X_j \\otimes A_R \\simeq 0$ for any $j$.*\n:::\n\nWe can now extend [1](#defi:borelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:borelcomplete\"} to the profinite case.\n\n::: defi\n**Definition 1**. *We define the $\\infty$-category of *Borel complete\n$R_G$-modules*\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$$\nas the full subcategory of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ on the\n$A_R$-complete $R_G$-modules. That is, an $R_G$-module $X$ is Borel\ncomplete if for all\n$Y \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ with\n$Y \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$ the mapping space\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(Y,X)$\nis contractible.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *As in the finite group case, the general theory of\n[@mnn17 §2.2] ensures that\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nis presentable and that its inclusion into\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ has a left adjoint\n$L_{G;R}$ we call *Borel completion*. There is a unique symmetric\nmonoidal structure on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nthat makes $L_{G;R}$ symmetric monoidal.\\\nHowever, a large proportion of the theory does not carry over, since\nthere is no reason for the algebra object $A_R$ that we defined as an\ninfinite colimit to be dualisable.[^8] In particular,\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nis not necessarily the right orthogonal to $A_R^{-1}$-local objects as\ndefined in [@mnn17 Definition 3.10], and we do not have nice\ndescriptions of the completion functor or the $\\infty$-category\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nas a functor category.*\n:::\n\nNevertheless, we can show a generalisation of\n[1](#cor:completionunderlying){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:completionunderlying\"} via an argument that always holds\nfor complete objects in module categories in the rigidly-compactly\ngenerated setting.\n\n::: {#lem:completionunderlyingprofinite .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *An $R_G$-module $X$ is Borel complete if and only if its\nunderlying $G$-spectrum $U_{R_G}(X) \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ is Borel\ncomplete.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* For ease of notation, we write $U=U_{R_G}$ and $F=F_{R_G}$. One\nimplication is as in\n[1](#rem:completeunderlyingeasydirection){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:completeunderlyingeasydirection\"}: Assume that the\n$R_G$-module $X$ is $A_R$-complete and let\n$Y \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ satisfy\n$Y \\otimes A_{\\mathbb{S}} \\simeq 0$. Then\n$F(Y) \\otimes_R A_R \\simeq F(Y) \\otimes_R F(A_{\\mathbb{S}}) \\simeq F(Y \\otimes A_{\\mathbb{S}}) \\simeq 0$\nand\n$$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(Y,U(X)) \\simeq \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(F(Y),X) \\simeq 0,$$\nhence $U(X)$ is $A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-complete. For the other direction, note\nthat by [@mnn17 §2.2] a map $f:U(X) \\to M$ of $G$-spectra exhibits $M$\nas the $A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-completion of $U(X)$ if and only if the\nfollowing two conditions are satisfied:\n\n1.  The map $f$ becomes an equivalence after tensoring with\n    $A_{\\mathbb{S}}$.\n\n2.  The $G$-spectrum $M$ is $A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-complete.\n\nLet $c: X \\to \\iota L_{G;R_G}(X)$ be the $A_R$-completion map for $X$.\nFrom the first part it follows that $U(\\iota L_{G;R_G}(X))$ is\n$A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-complete. Using the projection formula for the\nfree-forgetful adjunction the map $U(c) \\otimes A_{\\mathbb{S}}$\nidentifies with\n$$U(c \\otimes_R A_R): U(X \\otimes_R A_R) \\to U(\\iota L_{G;R_G}(X) \\otimes_R A_R),$$\nwhich is an equivalence since $c \\otimes_R A_R$ is one. Hence\n$U(c): U(X) \\to U\\iota L_{G;R_G}(X)$ exhibits $U\\iota L_{G;R_G}(X)$ as\nthe $A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-completion of $U(X)$. Now if $U(X)$ is\n$A_{\\mathbb{S}}$-complete then this map is an equivalence, and since $U$\nis conservative $c$ is an equivalence, which means that $X$ is\n$A_R$-complete, as desired. ◻\n:::\n\nWe finally connect the $\\infty$-category of Borel completes we just\ndefined to the previously defined $\\infty$-category of levelwise Borel\ncomplete modules.\n\n::: {#thm:borelandhyperlewelwise .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *There is an inclusion\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$\nwhich induces a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)^h_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}.$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We show that both categories agree as full subcategories of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$. Let\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$,\nwe first show that it is levelwise Borel complete. This is as in\n[1](#lem:categoricalfixedpointsborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:categoricalfixedpointsborelcomplete\"} - $X$ defines a\ncompatible family $(X^{N_i})_{i \\in I}$ for which we show that every\ncomponent is Borel complete. So for $i \\in I$ let\n$Y \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})$ such\nthat $\\textnormal{res}^{G_i}_1(Y) \\simeq 0$. Then\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(Y) \\simeq \\textnormal{res}^{G_i}_1(Y) \\simeq 0$\nand hence $\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(Y) \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$ by\n[1](#prop:noneqcontractibleprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:noneqcontractibleprofinite\"}. Then\n$$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})}(Y,X^{N_i}) \\simeq \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}(Y),X) \\simeq 0,$$\nso\n$X^{N_i} \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})$\nis Borel complete and $X$ is levelwise Borel. We hence have an inclusion\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\subseteq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}.$$\nNow, by definition\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$\nis hypercomplete if and only if the mapping space\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}}(Z,X)$\nis contractible for all acyclic $Z$, by\n[1](#prop:noneqcontractibleprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:noneqcontractibleprofinite\"} equivalently for all $Z$ of\nthe form $L_{\\textnormal{lw}}(Y)$ with $Y \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$\n(using that the levelwise completion is essentially surjective). By\nadjunction this holds for $X$ if and only if\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(Y,X)$\nis contractible for all $R_G$-modules $Y$ for which\n$Y \\otimes_{R_G} A_R \\simeq 0$ holds, which precisely means that $X$ is\nBorel complete. This shows that $X$ is in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nif and only if it is hypercomplete, and hence the two\n$\\infty$-categories in the statement agree as full subcategories of\n$R_G$-modules. Since they are both symmetric monoidal localisations of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ it follows from\nthe universal property of symmetric monoidal localisations [@hin16\nProposition 3.2.2] that the induced equivalence functor is symmetric\nmonoidal. ◻\n:::\n\nWe will see that under assumptions on $G$ and $R$ the $\\infty$-category\nof levelwise Borel complete $R_G$-modules is already hypercomplete, and\nhence in this case the two notions of Borel completeness we considered\nagree. We will discuss this in the next section.",
        "heading": "\\...and for profinite groups"
      },
      {
        "body_markdown": "In [@cm21 §4.1], Clausen and Mathew consider the classifying topos for a\nprofinite group and prove various results about hypercompleteness for\nsheaves of spectra on the latter. The purpose of this section is to\nconnect the previous results on Borel completeness for profinite groups\nto the results of Clausen and Mathew. We first recall some generalities.\n\n::: rec\n**Recollection 1**. *For a small $\\infty$-category $\\mathcal{C}$, we\ndenote by\n$\\mathcal{P}(C) = \\textnormal{Fun}(\\mathcal{C}^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}})$\nits *presheaf $\\infty$-category* and by\n$y: \\mathcal{C}\\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}(C)$ the Yoneda embedding. If\n$(\\mathcal{C}, \\tau)$ is an $\\infty$-site and $W$ is the class of\n$\\tau$-covering sieves $T \\to y(X)$ where $X \\in \\mathcal{C}$, then a\n*$\\tau$-sheaf on $\\mathcal{C}$* is a $W$-local object in\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$. The full subcategory\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C})$ of\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ spanned by such sheaves is the\n*$\\infty$-category of $\\tau$-sheaves on $\\mathcal{C}$*. We denote the\nleft adjoint sheafification functor by\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C})$.\\\nIf $W$ instead is the set of maps\n$\\textnormal{colim}_{[n] \\in \\Delta} \\; y(\\mathcal{U}_n) \\to y(X)$ for\n$\\mathcal{U}_{\\bullet}$ a hypercover of an object $X$, then an $W$-local\nobject of $\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ is called a *$\\tau$-hypersheaf on\n$\\mathcal{C}$*. The full subcategory of $\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ they\nspan is denoted\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C})$. Each\nhypersheaf is in particular a sheaf, and we denote the localisation\nfunctor by\n$(-)^{\\wedge}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C})$,\nthe composition with $\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}$ by\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}^{\\wedge}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{\\wedge}(\\mathcal{C})$.*\n:::\n\nReplacing $\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}$ by an $\\infty$-category with small\nlimits, we get the following.\n\n::: rec\n**Recollection 1**. *Let $(\\mathcal{C}, \\tau)$ be an $\\infty$-site and\nlet $\\mathcal{D}$ an $\\infty$-category with small limits. A\n*$\\tau$-(hyper)sheaf* on $\\mathcal{C}$ with values in $\\mathcal{D}$ is a\nfunctor $\\mathcal{F}: \\mathcal{C}^{\\textnormal{op}} \\to \\mathcal{D}$\nsuch that its canonical limit-preserving extension\n$\\bar{\\mathcal{F}}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})^{\\textnormal{op}} \\to \\mathcal{D}$\nfactors through the opposite of the localisation functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C})$.\nThe *$\\infty$-category of $\\tau$-(hyper)sheaves on $\\mathcal{C}$ with\nvalues in $\\mathcal{D}$* is the full subcategory\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\mathcal{C}; \\mathcal{D})$\nof\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})=\\textnormal{Fun}(\\mathcal{C}^{\\textnormal{op}},\\mathcal{D})$\non $\\tau$-(hyper)sheaves\n$\\mathcal{C}^{\\textnormal{op}} \\to \\mathcal{D}$.\\\nIf $\\mathcal{D}$ is furthermore presentable, then\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{\\wedge}(\\mathcal{C}; \\mathcal{D})$ is\npresentable and there is a left adjoint to the inclusion\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\mathcal{C}; \\mathcal{D}) \\subseteq \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$\ndenoted\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$.\nIf the topology is clear from the context we omit the $\\tau$ from the\nnotation.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:tstructureonsheaves .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *When\n$\\mathcal{D}= \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ for a\nconnective $\\mathbb{E}_{\\infty}$-ring $R$ we write\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};R)$ and\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ and for\nthe respective presheaf and (hyper)sheaf $\\infty$-categories with values\nin $R$-modules. By [@lur18 Proposition 1.3.2.7, 2.1.1.1] there is a\nt-structure on $\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ for\nwhich a sheaf $\\mathcal{F}$ is connective if the sheafification of the\npresheaf of abelian groups $X \\mapsto \\pi_n\\mathcal{F}(X)$ vanishes for\nall $n<0$ and it is coconnective if all its sections are after applying\nthe forgetful functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.\nThis t-structure is right complete and compatible with filtered\ncolimits.*\n:::\n\n::: {#prop:hypersheafhypercomplete .prop}\n**Proposition 1**. *A sheaf in\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ is a hypersheaf if\nand only if it is hypercomplete (in the sense of\n[1](#def:hypercompletetstructure){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"def:hypercompletetstructure\"}).*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* For sheaves of spectra this follows from [@lur09 Lemma\n6.5.3.11], [@dhi04; @tv03], [@lur09 Corollary 6.5.3.13] and [@lur18\nProposition 1.3.3.3], as discussed in [@cm21 Example 2.5]. We show that\nthe case with coefficients reduces to the one of spectral sheaves.\\\nSince the forgetful functor\n$U_R: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$\npreserves and detects limits, [@agv22 Remark 2.3.3] implies that the\ninduced functor\n$U_R: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};R) \\to \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\npreserves and detects sheaves and hypersheaves. Hence a sheaf in\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ is a hypersheaf if\nand only if it is one after applying $U_R$.\\\nIt remains to show the analogous statement for hypercomplete sheaves. It\nfollows from the description of the t-structure on\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ given in [@lur18\n§2.1.1] that the functor\n$U_R: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis t-exact. Under the identification\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$,\nwhere $\\underline{R}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf\nwith value $R$, the functor $U_R$ identifies with the forgetful functor\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nIt has a (automatically right t-exact) left adjoint we denote $F_R$, cf.\n[@lur18 Proposition 2.1.0.3]. Now the argument is analogous to the one\ngiven in\n[1](#lem:completionunderlyingprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:completionunderlyingprofinite\"} for complete objects in a\nmodule category.\\\nLet $\\mathcal{F}\\in \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; R)$ be\nhypercomplete. Then $U_R(\\mathcal{F})$ is hypercomplete. Indeed, if\n$\\mathcal{G}\\in \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis acyclic then $F_R(\\mathcal{G})$ is acyclic since $F_R$ is right\nt-exact and the t-structures at play are right complete. We have\n$$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}(\\mathcal{G},U_R(\\mathcal{F})) \\simeq \\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C};R)}(F_R(\\mathcal{F}),\\mathcal{G}) \\simeq 0,$$\nand hence $U_R(\\mathcal{F})$ is hypercomplete. For the other direction,\na map $f:U_R(\\mathcal{F}) \\to \\mathcal{M}$ of sheaves of spectra\nexhibits $\\mathcal{M}$ as the hypercompletion of $U_R(\\mathcal{F})$ if\nand only if the following two conditions are satisfied (cf. [@cm21\nProposition 2.32]):\n\n1.  The map $f$ is a $\\pi_{\\ast}$-isomorphism.\n\n2.  The sheaf $\\mathcal{M}$ is hypercomplete.\n\nLet $c: \\mathcal{F}\\to \\iota(\\mathcal{F}^h)$ be the hypercompletion map\nfor $\\mathcal{F}$. From the first part it follows that\n$U_R\\iota(\\mathcal{F}^h)$ is hypercomplete. Since $U_R$ commutes with\nhomotopy groups as a t-exact functor $U_R(c)$ is a\n$\\pi_{\\ast}$-isomorphism. Hence\n$U_R(c): U_R(\\mathcal{F}) \\to U_R(\\iota(\\mathcal{F}^h))$ exhibits\n$U_R(\\iota(\\mathcal{F}^h))$ as the hypercompletion of\n$U_R(\\mathcal{F})$. Now if $U_R(\\mathcal{F})$ is hypercomplete then this\nmap is an equivalence, and since $U_R$ is conservative $c$ is an\nequivalence, which means that $\\mathcal{F}$ is hypercomplete, which\nconcludes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: nota\n**Notation 1**. *For a profinite group $G$, we denote by\n$G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ the category of finite continuous $G$-sets\nendowed with the discrete topology and $G$-equivariant maps. It becomes\na site by declaring covering sieves to be families of jointly surjective\nmaps.*\n:::\n\nWhen $G$ is finite, the sheaf category with ring spectrum coefficients\nwe obtain for this site has a familiar description.\n\n::: {#lem:sheavesfunbg .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *Let $R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ be\nconnective and let $G$ be a finite group. Then there is a t-exact\nequivalence\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* This is [@cm21 Example 4.4], we just need to show that the\nequivalence is t-exact. Let\n$\\alpha: BG \\to G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}^\\textnormal{op}$ be the functor\nthat picks out the free $G$-set $G/1$. Then restriction along $\\alpha$\nand right Kan extension is an adjoint equivalence.\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=30, row sep=30]\n    & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} \\\\\n    {\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))} & {\\mathcal{P}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\alpha^*}\", shift right=3, shorten <=10pt, from=1-2, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"\\iota\", shift left=2, hook', from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\alpha_*}\", shift left=5, shorten >=10pt, from=2-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\"{marking, allow upside down}, shift left=4, draw=none, from=2-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=3, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}}\", shift left=2, from=2-2, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=4, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\hat{\\alpha}^*}\"', from=2-2, to=2-1]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ Here $\\textsf{\\textup{a}}$ is the sheafification functor\nand $\\hat{\\alpha}^*$ is the restriction along $\\alpha$ on presheaves. We\nhave $\\alpha^* \\simeq \\hat{\\alpha}^*\\iota$, and hence\n$\\alpha_* \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{a}}\\hat{\\alpha}_!$ by passing to left\nadjoints, where $\\hat{\\alpha}_!$ is the left adjoint of\n$\\hat{\\alpha}^*$. Here we use that $\\alpha_*$ is both left and right\nadjoint to $\\alpha^*$ since they are mutually inverse equivalences.\nSince $\\hat{\\alpha}^*$ is t-exact, $\\hat{\\alpha}_!$ is right t-exact,\nand since the sheafification $\\textsf{\\textup{a}}$ is t-exact it follows\nthat $\\alpha_*$ is right t-exact.\\\nOn the other hand, the right adjoint $\\hat{\\alpha}_*$ of\n$\\hat{\\alpha}^*$ already lands in sheaves, and hence $\\alpha_*$ factors\nas $\\textsf{\\textup{a}}\\hat{\\alpha}_*$. Again since $\\hat{\\alpha}^*$ is\nt-exact, $\\hat{\\alpha}_*$ is left t-exact, and hence $\\alpha_*$ is left\nt-exact as well, hence t-exact. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *It follows from [@cm21 Lemma 4.3] that the right Kan\nextension $\\alpha_*\\mathcal{F}$ of a functor\n$\\mathcal{F}: BG \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ to\n$G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}^\\textnormal{op}$ sends the $G$-set $G/H$ to the\n$H$-homotopy fixed points $\\mathcal{F}(\\ast_{BG})^{hH}$.*\n:::\n\nTogether with the observation that for a profinite group $G$, the site\n$G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ is a filtered colimit of the sites associated\nto the finite quotients of $G$, we get:\n\n::: {#prop:sheavesborelcomplete .prop}\n**Proposition 1**. *Let $R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nbe connective and let $G= \\textnormal{lim}_i \\, G_i$ be a profinite\ngroup. Then the inclusion of hypercomplete objects gives a commutative\ndiagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}}\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ in which both horizontal functors are symmetric monoidal\nequivalences.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We first consider the lower horizontal functor. By [@cm21\nConstruction 4.5] the site $G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ decomposes into a\nfiltered colimit of the $G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ along the canonical\nmaps $G_j\\textsf{\\textup{-set}} \\to G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ that\ninflate the $G_j$-action to a $G_i$-action along\n$G_i \\twoheadrightarrow G_j$ whenever $N_i \\subseteq N_j$. Then the\nsheaf category $\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$\ncan be written as the cofiltered\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{R}}$-limit\n$$\\textnormal{lim}_i \\; \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\stackrel{\\ref{lem:sheavesfunbg}}{\\simeq} \\textnormal{lim}_i \\; \\textnormal{Fun}(BG_i,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$$\nwith transition maps\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_j\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$\ngiven by restriction along the above functors of sites, cf. [@cm21\n§3.1]. In terms of the right-hand side, these are the maps\n$(-)^{h(N_j/N_i)}$. Passing to left adjoints, this is precisely the\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}})$-colimit that\ndefines\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$.\nBy [@lur18 Remark 1.3.2.8] the transition functors in the colimit\ndiagram for $\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$ are\nt-exact, hence the t-structure on the latter is the filtered colimit of\nthe t-structures on the\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$, as in\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"}. Since each of the\nequivalences coming from\n[1](#lem:sheavesfunbg){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:sheavesfunbg\"} is t-exact it follows that the equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$$\nis t-exact. Now the top horizontal equivalence follows from\n[1](#thm:borelandhyperlewelwise){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:borelandhyperlewelwise\"} and\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"} by passing to\nhypercomplete objects. ◻\n:::\n\nIn [@cm21 §4.1], it is studied when hypercompletion on\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis smashing, and criteria for sheaves of spectra to be hypercomplete in\nterms of weakly nilpotent group actions are given. Using this we can\ngive assumptions under which the vertical functors in\n[1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"} are actually equivalences. We\ndenote by $R^s$ the sheafification of the constant presheaf of spectra\nwith value $R$.\n\n::: {#prop:smashinghypercompletion .prop}\n**Proposition 1** (Clausen--Mathew). *Under each of the following\nassumptions the two vertical functors in\n[1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"} are equivalences:*\n\n1.  *The virtual cohomological dimension of $G$ is finite and $R^s$ is\n    hypercomplete. (The latter in particular holds when the ring\n    spectrum $R$ is truncated.)*\n\n2.  *The group $G$ has finite cohomological dimension $d$ and $R^s$\n    satisfies either of the two (equivalent) conditions:*\n\n    1.  *For every normal containment $N \\unlhd H$ of open subgroups the\n        spectrum with $H/N$-action $R^s(G/N)$ is d-nilpotent.*\n\n    2.  *There is a $d' \\geq 0$ such that for every open normal subgroup\n        $N \\unlhd G$ the spectrum with $G/N$-action $R^s(G/N)$ is\n        $d'$-nilpotent.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Part (1) is [@cm21 Corollary 4.28], see also [@cm21 Corollary\n4.29] for the statement about truncatedness. The second assertion\nfollows from the first and [@cm21 Theorem 4.26]. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Loosely speaking, the condition of $d$-nilpotency for a\nspectrum $X$ with an action of a finite group $G$ means that $X$ can be\nbuilt through retracts and extensions from an induced spectrum\n$\\oplus_G Y$ in $d+1$ many steps. For the precise definition we refer to\n[@cm21 Definition 4.18], see also [@mnn17; @mnn19]. The statement of\n[@cm21 Lemma 4.20] gives a characterisation in terms of the $d$-skeleton\nof the universal space for free $G$-actions $EG$.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *When $G$ is finite, the colimit diagram computing the\nlevelwise Borel complete category has a terminal object and\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}.$$\nNote also that the t-structure on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ is left complete, and\nhence the functor category\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$ is\nalready hypercomplete. This is consistent with part (1) of\n[1](#prop:smashinghypercompletion){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:smashinghypercompletion\"}, as in this case $R^s$ is\nhypercomplete since every object of\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$ is\nPostnikov-complete (that is, equivalent to the limit of its Postnikov\ntower).*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Under the assumption that the virtual cohomological\ndimension of $G$ is finite, Clausen and Mathew also show that\nhypercompletion on\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$ (for general\nconnective $R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$) is smashing\nand agrees with Postnikov completion [@cm21 Corollary 4.28, Proposition\n2.10]. In view of\n[1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"} this means that in this case the\nhypercompletion\n$$L^h: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$$\nis computed as the Postnikov completion\n$X \\mapsto \\lim_{n} \\tau_{\\leq n} X \\simeq X \\otimes \\lim_n \\tau_{\\leq n} R^s$.*\n:::\n\nWhen $R$ is a discrete commutative ring, we can give another description\nof the sheaf categories in\n[1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"}. As before, we write\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)$ for the (Grothendieck abelian) category of\ndiscrete $(G;R)$-modules, where $G$ is a profinite group, see e.g.\n[@bg23 §2]. Its derived $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ carries a natural t-structure\n[@lur17 Proposition 1.3.5.21], and although this t-structure is\ngenerally not left complete, $\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$\nis hypercomplete, since it has no nonzero acyclics.\n\n::: {#prop:sheavesgrmodules .prop}\n**Proposition 1**. *Let $R$ be a discrete commutative ring and let\n$G= \\textnormal{lim}_i \\, G_i$ be a profinite group. Then the inclusion\nof hypercomplete objects gives a commutative diagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))}\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ in which both horizontal functors are symmetric monoidal\nequivalences.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Again consider the colimit decomposition of\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$ from [@cm21\nConstruction 4.5]. For each $i \\in I$, we have\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}(BG_i,\\mathcal{D}(R)) \\simeq \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)),$$\nwhere the second equivalence follows from the identification of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)$ with modules over the group algebra\n$R[G_i]$ and the Schwede--Shipley theorem [@lur17 Theorem 7.1.2.1]. This\nequivalence is t-exact.\\\nThe functor\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_j\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$\nthat is left adjoint to the restriction along the inflation map\n$G_j\\textsf{\\textup{-set}} \\to G_i\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}$ for\n$N_i \\subseteq N_j$ corresponds to the functor on derived categories\ninduced by\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_j;R) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)$, the\nexact functor that inflates a $G_j$-action to a $G_i$-action along\n$G_i \\twoheadrightarrow G_j$. In terms of group algebras, this is a\nrestriction of scalars along the canonical map $R[G_i] \\to R[G_j]$. We\nhence obtain an equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)),$$\nwhere the colimit is taken in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}_{\\textnormal{st}})$\nalong the above maps. Using the same argument as in\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"} we obtain a\nt-structure on\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$ that\nis compatible with filtered colimits and has\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)$ as a heart. It makes the above equivalence\nt-exact. It remains to show that\n$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ identifies with the full\nsubcategory of hypercomplete objects of the above colimit.\\\nThe inflation functors\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)$ are exact\nand provide t-exact functors\n$\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i}: \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)) \\to \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$.\nThen there is an induced symmetric monoidal left adjoint\n$$\\alpha: \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)) \\to \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)).$$\nWrite\n$\\alpha_i: \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)) \\to \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$\nfor the canonical map and $\\beta_i$ for its right adjoint. Let\n$M \\in \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$.\nThen [@lur09 Lemma 6.3.3.6] implies that\n$M \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\alpha_i \\beta_i(M)$ and\n$\\alpha(M) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i} \\beta_i(M)$,\nso\n$$\\pi_*(\\alpha(M)) \\cong \\textnormal{colim}_i (\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G_i})^\\heartsuit \\pi_*(\\beta_i(M)) \\cong \\pi_*(M).$$\nIn particular, $\\alpha$ is t-exact. Since the t-structure on\n$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ is hypercomplete, we have that\n$$\\alpha(M) \\simeq 0 \\Leftrightarrow \\pi_*(\\alpha(M)) \\cong 0 \\Leftrightarrow \\pi_*(M) \\cong 0.$$\nThis means that the kernel of $\\alpha$ precisely consists of the acyclic\nobjects, and we need to show that the right adjoint of $\\alpha$ is fully\nfaithful. Denote by\n$\\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ the unseparated\nderived $\\infty$-category of [@lur18 §C.5.8]. There is a canonical\nlocalisation functor that quotients by the acyclic complexes\n$$\\tilde{\\alpha}: \\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)) \\twoheadrightarrow  \\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))/\\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))_{\\textnormal{ac}} \\simeq \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)).$$\nIts right adjoint is fully faithful and identifies the target with the\nhypercomplete objects of the source. Combining the universal property of\nthe prestable part of the unseparated derived $\\infty$-category [@lur18\nCorollary C.5.8.9] with [@lur18 Proposition C.3.1.1, C.3.2.1] we see\nthat $\\tilde{\\alpha}$ factors as $\\alpha \\circ \\check{\\alpha}$. Here\n$$\\check{\\alpha}: \\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)) \\to \\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$$\nis the unique t-exact left adjoint that is given by the identity on\nhearts. Note that $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)$ is itself the filtered\ncolimit of the categories $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)$ along the left\nexact left adjoint inflation functors\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_j;R) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)$ induced\nby the quotient maps $G_i \\twoheadrightarrow G_j$. So by [@lur18\nProposition C.5.5.20, C.3.3.5] we can also write\n$\\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ as a\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}$-colimit of the\n$\\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$, and the right\nadjoint of $\\check{\\alpha}$ is a\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{R}}$-limit of fully faithful functors\n$$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)) \\hookrightarrow \\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)).$$\nSo the right adjoints of $\\check{\\alpha}$ and $\\tilde{\\alpha}$ are fully\nfaithful, and hence the right adjoint of $\\alpha$ must be fully faithful\nas well. This finishes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Recall the classical equivalence\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)\\simeq \\textnormal{Sh}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$,\nwhere the latter is the 1-category of sheaves of (discrete) $R$-modules\non $G$-sets, and $G$ again is a profinite group. Then there is a fully\nfaithful embedding\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)\\simeq \\textnormal{Sh}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R),$$\nand by [@lur18 Corollary 2.1.2.3] it extends to a fully faithful functor\n$$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R)) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)$$\nwhich has essential image given by hypersheaves. This provides an\nalternative approach to the previous proposition.*\n:::\n\nIn this setting,\n[1](#prop:smashinghypercompletion){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:smashinghypercompletion\"} implies the following.\n\n::: {#cor:smashinghypercompletionreps .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *If the virtual cohomological dimension of the\nprofinite group $G$ is finite, the vertical functors in\n[1](#prop:sheavesgrmodules){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesgrmodules\"} are equivalences.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *By definition the unseparated derived $\\infty$-category\n$\\widecheck{\\mathcal{D}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ of [@lur18\nCorollary C.5.8.9] agrees with Krause's homotopy category of injectives\n$$\\mathcal{K}(\\textnormal{Inj} \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$$ of\n[@kra05; @kra15]. It generally differs from the filtered colimit of\nderived categories we considered above, this is already the case for\nfinite groups.\\\nWhen $G$ is finite, and when the coefficient ring $R$ is assumed regular\nand Noetherian, then a theorem of Mathew shows that\n$\\mathcal{K}(\\textnormal{Inj} \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ coincides\nwith the category of modules over the Borel completion of $R_G$ in\n$G$-spectra, which in this case also agrees with\n$\\textnormal{Ind}\\,\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Perf}}(R))$, see\n[@bar21 Theorem 3.7], [@tre15 Theorem A.4]. We refer to [@bchnl25 Remark\n3.35] for further discussion.*\n:::",
        "heading": "Sheaves and representations"
      },
      {
        "body_markdown": "We now start with the geometric part of the paper, in which we will\nconsider $\\infty$-categories of smooth Artin motives for the Nisnevich\nand the étale topology. They are constructed using the theory of finite\ncorrespondences [@cd19 §9]. For versions of (smooth) Artin motives for\nthe étale topology without correspondences we refer the reader to\n[@az12], [@rui25a; @rui25b].\\\nWe will work over a base scheme $S$ that we assume to be connected,\nnoetherian, and of finite Krull dimension.[^9] All morphisms of schemes\nare assumed to be separated and of finite type. In particular, all\nschemes considered are noetherian. Throughout, $R$ is a discrete\ncommutative ring.\n\n::: defi\n**Definition 1**. *Let $\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$ be the category of\nsmooth $S$-schemes with morphisms given by morphisms of $S$-schemes, and\nlet $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ be the full subcategory on finite étale\n$S$-schemes. The fibre product over $S$ endows both\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$ and $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ with a symmetric\nmonoidal structure which commutes with coproducts in both variables.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rec:cycles .rec}\n**Recollection 1** ([@cd19 §8.1.a]). *For a scheme $X$, a *cycle with\ndomain $X$* is a $\\mathbb{Z}$-linear combination of points of $X$. We\nwrite\n$$\\langle X \\rangle \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\sum_{x \\in X^{(0)}} \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X,x}).x$$ for the\n*cycle associated to $X$*.[^10] The sum runs over the generic\npoints[^11] of $X$. When $Z$ is a closed subscheme of a scheme $X$, the\ncycle $\\langle Z \\rangle$ is understood as a cycle with domain $X$. If\n$f: X \\to Y$ is a morphism of schemes, the *pushforward* of a cycle\n$\\alpha=\\sum_{i \\in I} n_ix_i$ with domain $X$ by $f$ is the cycle with\ndomain $Y$ given by $$f_*(\\alpha) = \\sum_{i \\in I} n_id_i.f(x_i),$$\nwhere $d_i$ is the degree of the extension $\\kappa(x_i)/\\kappa(f(x_i))$\nif it is finite and $0$ otherwise.*\n:::\n\n::: {#defi:correspondence .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth $S$-schemes. Then\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$, the group of *finite $S$-correspondences\nfrom $X$ to $Y$*, is the abelian group consisting of the finite and\nuniversally integral cycles over $S$ with domain $X \\times_S Y$.\\\nUsing each of the tensor products\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y) \\otimes R$ as hom-sets defines an additive\ncategory $\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$ which has objects the smooth\n$S$-schemes and morphisms the finite $S$-correspondences with\ncoefficients in $R$. Composition is defined using pushforward and\nintersection of cycles, and the identity of a smooth $S$-scheme $X$ is\ngiven by the cycle $\\langle \\Delta_X \\rangle$, where\n$\\Delta_X \\subseteq X\\times_S X$ is the diagonal [@cd19 §9.1].\\\nBy $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ we denote the full subcategory of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$ spanned by the finite étale $S$-schemes.\nFinite direct sums are given by the disjoint union of schemes, and the\nfibre product over $S$ endows both categories with an additively\nsymmetric monoidal structure [@cd19 §9.2].*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:nicecorrespondences .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *The definition given above is the most general one taken\nfrom [@cd19 §9.1], which goes back to [@sv00 §3], [@mvw06 Appendix 1A],\nand we will not need it in its full detail. We want to highlight three\nspecial cases of which the third one will be of importance later:*\n\n1.  *If the base scheme $S$ is regular, then\n    $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$ is the free abelian group on integral\n    closed subschemes $Z \\subseteq X \\times_S Y$ which are finite and\n    equidimensional over $X$ (that is, they are finite over $X$ and\n    dominate an irreducible component of $X$), see [@cd19 Remark 8.3.29,\n    9.1.3].*\n\n2.  *Assume that $X$ is smooth and $Y$ étale over $S$, write\n    $p_1: X \\times_S Y \\to X$ for the canonical (étale) morphism. Then\n    by [@cd19 Lemma 10.2.6] the group $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$ is\n    free abelian on the set of connected components $U$ of\n    $X \\times_S Y$ such that $p_1(U)$ is equal to a connected component\n    of $X$.*\n\n3.  *From (2) it follows that if $X$ is smooth and $Y$ finite étale over\n    $S$, then $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$ is the free abelian group\n    on the connected components $X \\times_S Y$, cf. [@cd19 Proposition\n    10.2.5].*\n\n*The apparent discrepancy between (1) and (2) can be explained as\nfollows: every connected scheme $X$ that is smooth over a regular and\nhence normal scheme $S$ is already itself normal, and since it is\nassumed noetherian it is integral.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *In [@cd19 §9] finite correspondences with coefficients in\na ring $R$ are defined by means of $\\Lambda$-universal cycles, where\n$\\Lambda \\subseteq \\mathbb{Q}$ is the localisation of $\\mathbb{Z}$ at\nthe integers that are invertible in $R$. By [@cd19 Remark 9.1.3]\ntensoring the resulting correspondence groups over $\\Lambda$ with $R$\nresults in the hom-modules of $\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$ defined\nabove.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:isoetalecorrespondences .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *The identification made in (2) of\n[1](#rem:nicecorrespondences){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:nicecorrespondences\"} poses a subtlety: it identifies\nconnected components with the sum of their generic points. For example,\nthe identity of $S$ in $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(S,S)$ is given by\n$\\langle \\Delta_S \\rangle$, but if $S$ is only connected but not\nirreducible $\\Delta_S \\cong S$ can have multiple irreducible components.\nUnder the identification made in (2) the cycle\n$\\langle \\Delta_S \\rangle$ corresponds to the unique connected component\nof $S \\times_S S$. In fact, the proof of [@cd19 Lemma 10.2.6] shows that\nfor $X$ a smooth and $Y$ an étale $S$-scheme the map\n$$\\mathbb{Z}[\\pi_0^{\\textnormal{fin}}(X \\times_S Y/X)] \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y), \\; U \\mapsto \\langle U \\rangle = \\sum_{u \\in U^{(0)}} \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{U,u}).u$$\nis an isomorphism, where $\\pi_0^{\\textnormal{fin}}(X \\times_S Y/X)$ is\nthe set of connected components $U$ of $X \\times_S Y$ such that the\nprojection $p_1(U)$ is equal to a connected component of $X$. When $Y$\nis finite étale over $S$ the condition on the projection can be\ndropped.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rec:graphfunctors .rec}\n**Recollection 1**. *Let $f: X \\to Y$ be a morphism of smooth\n$S$-schemes. Then its graph $\\Gamma_f$ is a closed subscheme of\n$X \\times_S Y$, and by [@cd19 Example 9.1.4] the cycle\n$\\langle \\Gamma_f \\rangle$ with domain $X \\times_S Y$ defines an element\nof $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$. This construction gives faithful\nfunctors\n$\\gamma: \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S\\to \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$ and\n$\\gamma: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ which\nare the identity on objects and take a morphism of $S$-schemes\n$f: X \\to Y$ to the cycle $\\langle \\Gamma_f \\rangle$. They are symmetric\nmonoidal [@cd19 9.2.4].*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Using the description of correspondence groups given in\n[1](#rem:nicecorrespondences){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:nicecorrespondences\"} it follows that all objects of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ are self-dual with respect to the\nsymmetric monoidal structure of\n[1](#defi:correspondence){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:correspondence\"}.*\n:::\n\n::: nota\n**Notation 1**. *In what follows, $\\tau$ will denote either the étale or\nthe Nisnevich topology on $\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$ or a full subcategory\nthereof. For the former, covering families are finite families\n$(X_i \\to X)_{i \\in I}$ of étale morphisms that are jointly surjective,\nand for the latter we furthermore demand that for every $x \\in X$ there\nexists $i \\in I$ and $x_i \\in X_i$ mapping to $x$ such that the induced\nmap of residue fields $\\kappa(x) \\to \\kappa(x_i)$ is an isomorphism.\\\nFor $\\mathcal{C}$ an additive $\\infty$-category (which in our case will\nbe a correspondence category) we will write\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ for the\n$\\infty$-category of additive presheaves on $\\mathcal{C}$ with values in\nspectra. We refer to Appendix\n[6](#sec:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"sec:sheaveswithtransfers\"} for some recollections.*\n:::\n\n::: {#defi:sheaveswithtransfers .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *The objects of\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nare called *presheaves with transfers*. We define the $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nof *$\\tau$-(hyper)sheaves with transfers* as the pullback\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),}\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}^{(\\wedge),\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\tau}}\", hook]\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1, \"\\gamma^*\"]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2, \"\\hat{\\gamma}^*\"]\n    \\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}}\", hook]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ where the horizontal functors are the canonical\ninclusions and vertical functors precompose with the graph functor\n$\\gamma: \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S\\to \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$. When\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$ is replaced by $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ we\ndenote the resulting sheaf category by\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.*\n:::\n\nNote that in the above pullback we use that sheaves for both topologies\nalready preserve finite products, see e.g. [@lur18 Proposition A.3.3.1].\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Under our assumptions on the base scheme $S$ the\nNisnevich topos\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S)$\nis hypercomplete, which follows from [@lur18 Theorem 3.7.7.1] or [@cm21\nTheorem 3.18] using the argument given in [@mat24 Lemma 5.1].\nFurthermore, by [@lur18 Proposition 1.3.3.3] a sheaf of spectra is a\nhypersheaf if and only if the underlying sheaf of spaces is one, so we\ndo not need to distinguish between sheaves and hypersheaves for the\nNisnevich topology.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:tstructuresheaveswithtransfers .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *In the étale case, we can express hypersheaves with\ntransfers as the iterated pullback $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge,\\textnormal{tr}}}\", hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\gamma^*}\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}}\", hook, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\gamma^*}\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\hat{\\gamma}^*}\", from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}}\", hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", hook, from=2-2, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-2, to=2-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ Recall from\n[1](#prop:hypersheafhypercomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:hypersheafhypercomplete\"} that hypercomplete sheaves are\nprecisely the hypercomplete objects in sheaves. There is a right\ncomplete t-structure on sheaves with transfers which makes the functor\n$\\gamma^*$ to sheaves t-exact (see\n[1](#rem:tstrucuresonsheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:tstrucuresonsheaveswithtransfers\"}), and hypersheaves\nwith transfers are precisely the hypercomplete objects with respect to\nthis t-structure, by essentially the same argument as in\n[1](#prop:hypersheafhypercomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:hypersheafhypercomplete\"}.\\\nIn view of [1](#rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback\"} all the functors in the\ndiagram above have left adjoints, and in particular hypercompletion on\nétale sheaves induces a left adjoint on étale sheaves with transfers\n$$(-)^\\wedge_\\textnormal{ét}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^\\wedge(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:representables .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *For a smooth (resp. finite étale) $S$-scheme $X$ the\npresheaf with transfers\n$$R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X) \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\bar{y}(X) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(-,X) \\otimes R$$ is an étale\nhypersheaf with transfers, where\n$\\bar{y}: \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\n(resp.\n$\\bar{y}: \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$)\nis the stable Yoneda embedding of\n[1](#rec:psigma){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"rec:psigma\"},\nwhich follows from [@cd16 Proposition 2.1.4], see also [@bh21 Remark\n14.6]. This gives an induced symmetric monoidal functor\n$$R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S: \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nand replacing $\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}$ by $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}$ gives\nits analogue for finite étale schemes.*\n:::\n\n::: {#defi:motives .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *The $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$ of *effective\n$\\tau$-motives* is the full subcategory of\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\non the $\\mathcal{S}$-local objects, where $\\mathcal{S}$ is the\ncollection of morphisms\n$R^\\textnormal{tr}_S(\\mathbb{A}^1_X) \\to R^\\textnormal{tr}_S(X)$ for\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_{S}$. We denote the compact part\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)^{\\omega}$ by\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff,gm}, (\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$, its objects\nare called *geometric* motives.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *By [@lur09 Proposition 5.5.4.15] the $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$ is presentable\nand a localisation of\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.\nWe could also define it as a further pullback along the inclusion of\n$\\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves with transfers into the latter. We\nwrite\n$$L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$$\nfor the left adjoint localisation functor. By\n[1](#rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback\"},\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nhas a symmetric monoidal structure, and using [@lur17 Proposition\n2.2.1.9] one can check that the functor $L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}$ above is a\nsymmetric monoidal localisation. We obtain a symmetric monoidal\ncomposition\n$$\\mathcal{M}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}: \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S\\stackrel{\\gamma}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R) \\stackrel{R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\stackrel{L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R),$$\nand for $X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$ we call\n$\\mathcal{M}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(X)$ the *effective motive associated to\n$X$*. For the Nisnevich topology, it follows from the finite\ncohomological dimension of the base scheme [@ks86 1.2.5] that\n$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R)$ is compactly\ngenerated by the motives $\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(X)$ for $X$\nsmooth over $S$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#defi:smoothartinmotives .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *The $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(S;R)$ of *smooth Artin $\\tau$-motives*\nis defined as the localising subcategory of\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$ generated by the\nmotives associated to finite étale $S$-schemes.
