We denote the compact\npart $\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(S;R)^{\\omega}$ by\n$\\mathcal{DAM}^{\\textnormal{gm}, (\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$, its objects are\ncalled *geometric smooth Artin motives*.*\n:::\n\nAs in the Nisnevich case the generators of\n$\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$ are compact we can also describe\nthe latter as the thick subcategory of\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff,gm}}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$ generated\nby the motives associated to finite étale $S$-schemes, using\nNeeman--Thomason localisation. Since the motives associated to finite\nétale schemes are self-dual, in particular dualisable,\n$\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$ is rigidly compactly generated.\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Recall that one passes from effective motives\n$\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$ to non-effective\nmotives $\\mathcal{DM}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(S;R)$ by tensor inverting the\neffective motive associated to the motivic sphere\n$\\mathbb{S}^{\\mathbb{A}^1} = \\textnormal{cofib}(\\mathcal{M}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(S) \\to \\mathcal{M}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\mathbb{G}_{m,S}))$.\nHere the map $S \\to \\mathbb{G}_{m,S}$ is the constant section with value\n$1$ of the canonical map $\\mathbb{G}_{m,S} \\to S$. In general the\nquestion when the functor from effective to non-effective motives is\nfully faithful is subtle, see e.g. [@voe00 Theorem 4.3.1], [@voe10],\n[@cd19 Corollary 11.2.15]. In this paper we will only deal with\neffective motives.*\n:::\n\n::: {#cons:fettosm .cons}\n**Construction 1**. *The inclusion functor\n$\\iota: \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$\ninduces an adjunction\n$$(\\hat{\\iota}_!,\\hat{\\iota}^*): \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nof categories of presheaves with transfers. Here $\\hat{\\iota}^*$ is\nrestriction along $\\iota$, and $\\hat{\\iota}_!$ is given by left Kan\nextension along $\\iota$, which restricts to $\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(-;R)$\nby [@chll24 Proposition 3.3.2]. The pointwise formula for the left Kan\nextension\n$$\\hat{\\iota}_!F(Y) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_{(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)^\\textnormal{op})_{/Y}} \\; F$$\nensures that\n$\\hat{\\iota}_!(R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)) \\simeq R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)$\nholds for a finite étale scheme $X$.*\n:::\n\nFix a geometric point $s$ of the base scheme $S$, i.e. a morphism\n$s: \\textnormal{Spec}(k) \\to S$ where $k$ is an algebraically closed\nfield. From now on, write $G$ for $\\pi^{\\textnormal{ét}}_1(S,s)$, the\nétale fundamental group of the base scheme [@sga1]. We write\n$\\underline{R}$ for the Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum of the constant\nMackey functor associated to the ring $R$ and\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R)$ for the additive category of\n$(G;R)$-permutation modules [@bg23 §2]. Our aim now is to extend\nVoevodsky's theorem [@voe00 §3.4] that expresses Artin motives over a\nfield in terms of permutation modules.\n\n::: {#thm:damnisasmodunderlr .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *There is a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\simeq \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We first produce a left adjoint\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\to \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$\nand then apply the Barr-Beck theorem. Using [@bcn25 Example 2.15] or\n[@fuh25 Corollary 3.18] we can work with\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\ninstead of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\nthroughout. Recall Grothendieck's equivalence of finite discrete\n$G$-sets and finite étale $S$-schemes from [@sga1], and consider the\nsymmetric monoidal functor defined on 1-categories of spans thereof:\n$$\\begin{align*}\n\\Psi: \\textsf{\\textup{span}}(G) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{span}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R).\n\\end{align*}$$ It is the identity on objects and sends a span of finite\nétale $S$-schemes, represented by a map $f: U \\to X \\times_S Y$, to the\npushforward correspondence\n$$f_*\\langle U \\rangle = \\sum_{u \\in U^{(0)}} \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{U,u}) \\cdot d_u. f(u).$$\nBy [@cd19 9.1.1, Lemma 10.2.6] the cycle $f_*\\langle U \\rangle$ is an\nelement of $\\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,Y)$. The identity span\n$(X \\to X \\times_S X)$ is sent to\n$\\langle \\Delta_X \\rangle = \\textnormal{id}_X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(X,X)$,\nand composition of finite correspondences as described in [@cd19\nDefinition 9.1.5] makes $\\Psi$ functorial. It preserves finite\ncoproducts and hence extends to a functor\n$$\\Psi: \\Omega(G) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R),$$ where $\\Omega(G)$\nis the Burnside category of finite $G$-sets obtained by group completing\nthe hom-sets in $\\textsf{\\textup{span}}(G)$ that are abelian monoids\nunder disjoint union. There is a 'cohomological' ideal $\\mathcal{I}(G)$\nof homomorphisms in $\\Omega(G)$ that is generated by elements\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:cohidealgeneator}\n(G/H \\stackrel{\\pi^H_K}{\\longleftarrow} G/K \\stackrel{\\pi^H_K}{\\longrightarrow} G/H) - ([H:K] \\cdot \\textnormal{id}_{G/H})\n\\end{equation}$$ for a pair of open subgroups $K \\leq H \\leq G$, see\n[@bg23 §4]. The left-hand span in\n[\\[eq:cohidealgeneator\\]](#eq:cohidealgeneator){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:cohidealgeneator\"} corresponds to a span of finite étale\n$S$-schemes $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:spangenerator}\n(X/\\overline{H} \\stackrel{\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}}{\\longleftarrow} X/\\overline{K} \\stackrel{\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}}{\\longrightarrow} X/\\overline{H})\n\\end{equation}$$ for some finite étale cover $X \\to S$ which can be\nchosen so that the kernel of the canonical homomorphism\n$\\varphi: G \\to \\textnormal{Aut}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S}(X)$ is\ncontained in $K$, hence in $H$, and $\\overline{H}$, $\\overline{K}$ are\nthe respective images of $H$ and $K$ under $\\varphi$. The map\n$\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}$ is the canonical projection, induced\nby the universal property of the quotient by a group action [@gw23\nProposition 20.87]. We now show that the generators in\n[\\[eq:cohidealgeneator\\]](#eq:cohidealgeneator){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:cohidealgeneator\"} and hence the ideal $\\mathcal{I}(G)$\nare killed by the functor $\\Psi$.\\\nLet $f: X/\\overline{K} \\to X/\\overline{H} \\times_S X/\\overline{H}$\ncorrespond to the span\n[\\[eq:spangenerator\\]](#eq:spangenerator){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:spangenerator\"}. It factors through the diagonal\n$\\Delta_{X/\\overline{H}} \\subseteq X/\\overline{H} \\times_S X/\\overline{H}$\nwhich is isomorphic to $X/\\overline{H}$. We thus have a commutative\ndiagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {X/\\overline{K}} & {\\Delta_{X/\\overline{H}}} & {X/\\overline{H} \\times_S X/\\overline{H}.} \\\\\n    & {X/\\overline{H}}\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"f\", bend left=20, from=1-1, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-2, \"\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}\"']\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2, \"\\hspace*{-0.01cm}\\rotatebox{90}{$\\sim$}\"]\n    \\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-2, \"p_1\"]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ It hence suffices to show that\n$(\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}})_*\\langle X/\\overline{K} \\rangle = [H:K] . \\langle X/\\overline{H} \\rangle$\nholds. The canonical projection\n$\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}: X/\\overline{K} \\to X/\\overline{H}$\nis surjective and thus maps generic points to generic points. Let $y$ be\na generic point of $X/\\overline{H}$. Then the coefficient of $y$\nappearing in the cycle\n$(\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}})_*\\langle X/\\overline{K} \\rangle$ is\n$$\\begin{align*}\n\\sum_{x} \\; [\\kappa(x) : \\kappa(y)] \\; \\cdot \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X/\\overline{K},x}) &= \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X/\\overline{H},y}) \\cdot \\sum_{x} \\; [\\kappa(x) : \\kappa(y)] \\tag*{\\cite[{}10.52.13]{stacks}} \\\\\n&= \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X/\\overline{H},y}) \\cdot \\textnormal{deg}(\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}}) \\tag*{\\cite[Prop. 12.21]{gw10}}\\\\\n&= \\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X/\\overline{H},y}) \\cdot [H:K] \\tag*{\\cite[Prop. 20.89]{gw23}}\n\\end{align*}$$ where the sum runs over all\n$x \\in (\\pi^{\\overline{H}}_{\\overline{K}})^{-1}(y)$. Since\n$\\textnormal{lg}(\\mathcal{O}_{X/\\overline{H},y})$ is precisely the\ncoefficient of $y$ in $\\langle \\Delta_{X/\\overline{H}} \\rangle$ it\nfollows that\n$$\\Psi(f) = f_* \\langle X/\\overline{K} \\rangle = [H:K] . \\langle \\Delta_{X/\\overline{H}} \\rangle = [H:K] . \\textnormal{id}_{X/\\overline{H}}.$$\nHence $\\Psi$ descends to $\\Omega(G)/\\mathcal{I}(G)$. Since the target\n$\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ is $R$-linear, we can extend the source\nto $\\Omega_R(G)/\\mathcal{I}_R(G)$, as in [@bg23 Corollary 4.21]. Here\n$\\Omega_R(G)$ is the $R$-linearisation of $\\Omega(G)$, and\n$\\mathcal{I}_R(G)$ is the analogous ideal of $\\Omega_R(G)$ on the same\ngenerators as for $\\mathcal{I}(G)$. By [@bg23 Proposition 4.17] the free\n$R$-module functor induces an equivalence\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R)\\simeq \\Omega_R(G)/\\mathcal{I}_R(G)$, and we\nhave an additive symmetric monoidal functor\n$$\\psi: \\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R)\\stackrel{\\Psi}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\stackrel{\\iota}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R),$$\nwhere the second functor is the canonical inclusion. Using [@chll24\nProposition 3.3.2] restriction and left Kan extension provide an\nadjunction\n$$(\\psi_!, \\psi^*): \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nIf we write\n$\\iota_!: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nfor the functor given by the composition of $\\hat{\\iota}_!$ (left Kan\nextension on $\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}$, see\n[1](#cons:fettosm){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"cons:fettosm\"})\nand sheafification it makes the following diagram commute:\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) & \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R) \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[\"\\iota\", hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\iota_!}\", shift left, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ Hence, the composition\n$L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}\\psi_!$\nlands in the full subcategory $\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$ of\n$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R)$. Composing\n$(\\psi_!, \\psi^*)$ with the adjunctions\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=1.4cm]\n    {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R)}\n    \\arrow[\"{(\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{tr}},\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{tr}})}\", shift left, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[shift left=2, from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{(L_{\\mathbb{A}^1},\\textnormal{incl})}\", shift left, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift left, from=1-3, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ we thus obtain an adjunction\n$$(\\alpha, \\beta): \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G);R) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R).$$\nNow, $\\alpha$ sends the presheaf associated to a finite $G$-set (i.e.,\nits free $\\underline{R}$-module) to the motive associated to its\ncorresponding finite étale $S$-scheme. By construction $\\alpha$ is\nsymmetric monoidal, so it preserves dualisable and hence compact\nobjects, and it sends a set of generators to a set of generators. It\nfollows that $\\beta$ preserves colimits and is conservative. Since the\nprojection formula holds automatically in this case, [@mnn17 Proposition\n5.29] gives a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}(S)})}\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}(S)})}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G),$$\nwhere the second equivalence is [@lur17 Corollary 3.4.1.9]. It remains\nto identify the algebra object\n$\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))$. For some open subgroup\n$H \\leq G$, the $n$-th homotopy is given by $$\\begin{align}\n\\pi_n^{H}(\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))) &= \\textnormal{Hom}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty +n}_+G/H \\otimes \\underline{R},\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))) \\notag \\\\\n&\\cong \\textnormal{Hom}_{\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)}(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(X/\\overline{H}),\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S)), \\label{eq:homotopy}\n\\end{align}$$ where $X/\\overline{H}$ is the finite étale $S$-scheme\ncorresponding to the $G$-set $G/H$ - here $X$ is a finite étale\n$S$-scheme chosen so that $H$ contains the kernel of the canonical\nhomomorphism $G \\to \\textnormal{Aut}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S}(X)$, and\n$\\overline{H}$ is the image of $H$ under this homomorphism. By [@cd19\nTheorem 11.2.14, Proposition 10.2.5] the group\n[\\[eq:homotopy\\]](#eq:homotopy){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:homotopy\"} is isomorphic to $R$ when $n=0$, and zero\notherwise. Furthermore, for an inclusion of open subgroups $H \\leq K$ of\n$G$ the restriction map\n$$\\pi_n^{K}(\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))) \\to \\pi_n^{H}(\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S)))$$\nis given by precomposition with the map of motives that comes from the\ncanonical degree $[K:H]$-map $X/\\overline{H} \\to X/\\overline{K}$, where\n$X$ is chosen such that the kernel of\n$G \\to \\textnormal{Aut}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S}(X)$ contains $K$ and\nhence $H$. Again by [@cd19 Theorem 11.2.14, Proposition 10.2.5] in\ndegree $0$ this identifies with the map\n$$R(\\pi_0(X/\\overline{H})) \\to R(\\pi_0(X/\\overline{K})),$$ which is the\nidentity since both schemes are connected. It follows that there is an\nabstract equivalence\n$\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S)) \\cong \\underline{R}$ (note\nthat [@cd19 Proposition 11.2.5] is precisely the statement that the\nresulting Mackey functor is cohomological [@tw95 §16]). We need to show\nthat it is induced by a map of algebra objects.\\\nConsider the unit map\n$\\varphi: \\underline{R} \\to \\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))$.\nSince both algebra objects live in the heart\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)^{\\heartsuit} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mack}}_R^{\\textsf{\\textup{coh}}}(G)$,\nthe map $\\varphi$ is induced by an algebra map in the heart\n$\\varphi^{\\heartsuit}: \\underline{R}^\\heartsuit \\to \\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S))^\\heartsuit$.\nSince both sides are isomorphic to the Mackey functor $\\underline{R}$\nand the latter is the initial commutative cohomological Green functor,\n$\\varphi^\\heartsuit$ is an isomorphism, and $\\varphi$ is an equivalence\nof commutative algebra objects. Hence, we have\n$\\beta(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S)) \\simeq \\underline{R}$ in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$. This concludes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Using the spectral Mackey functor description of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$, we could also produce a left adjoint from the\nlatter to $\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$, in fact with less\nwork on finite correspondences. Then the Barr-Beck theorem applies, but\nthe difficulty then lies in identifying the algebra object we obtain by\napplying the right adjoint to the unit. This identification is simpler\nwhen we already deal with an $\\underline{R}$-module.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Another way to obtain a functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G\\to \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)$ is\nconstructing a functor\n$c_S: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G\\to \\mathcal{SH}^\\textnormal{eff}(S)$ to\neffective motivic spectra over $S$, and then passing to effective\nmotives. Over a field, such a functor has been constructed by\nHeller--Ormsby [@ho16], for a much more general construction see [@bh21\n§10.2].\\\nIn the case of the real and the complex numbers, it is known\n[@lev14; @ho16; @ho18] that these functors (now with values in all of\n$\\mathcal{SH}$) restrict to equivalences\n$$c_{\\mathbb{C}}: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}\\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{SH}_{\\textnormal{A}}(\\mathbb{C}) \\hspace{1cm} \\textnormal{and} \\hspace{1cm} c_{\\mathbb{R}}: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{C_2} \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow}\\mathcal{SH}_{\\textnormal{A}}(\\mathbb{R})$$\nonto the localising subcategories generated by motivic spectra\nassociated to finite étale algebras for the respective fields. The\ninverses are given by complex and real Betti realisation, which are\ninduced by the assignment that sends a complex (resp. real) variety to\nits complex (resp. real) points. Combining this with the fact that\n$C_2$-equivariant Betti realisation sends the motivic cohomology\nspectrum associated to $\\mathbb{Z}$ to the constant Mackey functor\n$\\underline{\\mathbb{Z}}$ [@ho16 Theorem 4.17], the compatibility of this\nwith restriction [@bhs22 Recollection 1.19] and the fact that motives\nover a field of characteristic zero are modules over motivic cohomology\n[@ro08] we obtain induced equivalences\n$$c_{\\mathbb{C}}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{Z}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\mathbb{C};\\mathbb{Z}) \\hspace{0.5cm} \\textnormal{and} \\hspace{0.5cm} c_{\\mathbb{R}}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{\\mathbb{Z}}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{C_2}) \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\mathbb{R};\\mathbb{Z}).$$\nNote that over a field, we do not need to distinguish between effective\nand non-effective Artin motives [@bg23 Remark 7.9].*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:alternativeproof .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *One can also show directly that\n$\\Psi: \\textsf{\\textup{span}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$\nwhich we used above induces an equivalence\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R)\\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ upon\nfactoring out the cohomological ideal, see [@bg23 Proposition 4.17] and\nthe ideas indicated in [@bg23 Remark 6.5]. From there one can pursue a\nsimilar proof strategy as in op. cit. by showing that since Nisnevich\ncovers of finite étale schemes split, a presheaf with transfers on\nfinite étale schemes is automatically a Nisnevich sheaf. Then one can\nargue that these sheaves embed fully faithfully into Nisnevich sheaves\nwith transfers on smooth schemes and are not affected by\n$\\mathbb{A}^1$-localisation.*\n:::\n\nHaving dealt with the Nisnevich case, we now consider the étale\ntopology. The following considerations also hold for the Nisnevich\ntopology, but we will stick to the former in terms of notation, since\nthat is the case in which they will be applied.\n\n::: {#lem:restrictionsheaves .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *The restriction functor $\\hat{\\iota}^*$ from\n[1](#cons:fettosm){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"cons:fettosm\"}\npreserves (hyper)sheaves with transfers and hence induces a functor\n$$\\iota^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* First, note that the restriction\n$\\hat{i}^*:\\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nalong the inclusion\n$i: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$\npreserves (hyper)sheaves, since\n$i: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S$\npreserves covers. We thus have an induced functor\n$i^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.\nSince there is a commutative square $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S& \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S\\\\\n    \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) & \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R),\n    \\arrow[\"i\", hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\gamma\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\gamma\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\iota\", hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ the universal property of the pullback squares defining\nsheaves with transfers using the functor $i^*$ together with the\nrestriction functors on presheaves and presheaves with transfers induces\na functor\n$$\\iota^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nwhich is given by restricting the functor $\\hat{\\iota}^*$ on presheaves\nwith transfers to sheaves with transfers. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *The functor\n$\\iota^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nhas a left adjoint $\\iota_!$ given by\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge), \\textnormal{tr}} \\hat{\\iota}_!$,\nas in the proof of\n[1](#thm:damnisasmodunderlr){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:damnisasmodunderlr\"}. In particular, the property\n$\\iota_!(R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)) \\simeq R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)$ for\n$X$ finite étale over $S$ also holds on (hyper)sheaves with transfers.*\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:iotastar .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *The functor $\\iota^*$ from\n[1](#lem:restrictionsheaves){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:restrictionsheaves\"} preserves colimits.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* As a right adjoint between stable $\\infty$-categories $\\iota^*$\nis exact. We hence need to show that $\\iota^*$ preserves filtered\ncolimits. Filtered colimits in\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nand\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nare computed pointwise and $\\hat{\\iota}^*$ preserves them. Colimits in\n(hyper)sheaves with transfers are computed as the (hyper)sheafification\nof the colimit taken in presheaves. By\n[1](#lem:restrictionsheaves){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:restrictionsheaves\"} the functor $\\iota^*$ is the\nrestriction of $\\hat{\\iota}^*$ to (hyper)sheaves with transfers, which\nimplies the claim. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:inclusionderived .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *The functor\n$\\iota_!: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis fully faithful and symmetric monoidal.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* To show that $\\iota_!$ is fully faithful we consider the unit\n$\\textnormal{id} \\to \\iota^*\\iota_!$ of the adjunction\n$\\iota_! \\dashv \\iota^*$. By\n[1](#lem:iotastar){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"lem:iotastar\"}\nthe restriction $\\iota^*$ preserves colimits, $\\iota_!$ preserves\ncolimits as a left adjoint, and\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis generated by 'representables' $R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)$ under\ncolimits and shifts. This means that in order to show that\n$\\textnormal{id} \\to \\iota^*\\iota_!$ is an equivalence it suffices to\nevaluate on objects $R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)$ for $X$ a finite étale\n$S$-scheme. In this case we have\n$\\iota^*\\iota_!(R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(X)) \\simeq \\iota^*(R_S^{\\textnormal{tr}}(X)) \\simeq R_S^{\\textnormal{tr}}(X)$,\nand we conclude that $\\iota_!$ is fully faithful.\\\nThe symmetric monoidal structure on presheaves with transfers is\nobtained by localising the Day convolution on presheaves, so as\n$\\iota: \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$\nis symmetric monoidal with respect to the monoidal structure of [@cd19\n§9.2], the left adjoint on presheaves with transfers $\\hat{\\iota}_!$ is\nas well [@bs24 Proposition 3.6]. Since the symmetric monoidal structure\non (hyper)sheaves with transfers is obtained by localising the symmetric\nmonoidal structure on presheaves with transfers, the\n(hyper)sheafification functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}$ is symmetric\nmonoidal, and so is\n$\\iota_! = \\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge), \\textnormal{tr}}\\hat{\\iota}_!$. ◻\n:::\n\nIn the hypercomplete case, we can give assumptions under which the\ncomposition of the functor $\\iota_!$ with $\\mathbb{A}^1$-localisation to\neffective motives stays fully faithful, here computations of étale\ncohomology are at hand (see the comparison to the classical setup in\nAppendix [6](#sec:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"sec:sheaveswithtransfers\"}).\n\n::: {#lem:aonelocalisationetale .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *If the ring $R$ has positive characteristic $n$ and the\nresidue characteristics of $S$ are prime to $n$, then the functor\n$$\\iota_!: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nremains fully faithful after composing it with the\n$\\mathbb{A}^1$-localisation functor\n$$L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\twoheadrightarrow \\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* As in the proof of [@bg23 Proposition 7.4], using [@cd16\nProposition 2.2.3], it suffices to show that for any finite étale\n$S$-scheme $Y$ and any smooth $S$-scheme $X$ the canonical map\n$$\\textnormal{H}^i_{\\textnormal{ét}}(X \\times_S Y,R) \\to \\textnormal{H}^i_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\mathbb{A}^1_{X \\times_S Y},R)$$\nis an isomorphism in all degrees. The map $X \\times_S Y \\to X$ and hence\nits pullback to $\\mathbb{A}^1_X$ are étale, and the residue\ncharacteristics of $X$ can only be those of $S$. We can then invoke\n[@cd16 Theorem 1.3.2], as in [@cd16 Proposition 3.1.7]. ◻\n:::\n\nThe following can be interpreted as a weak form of the rigidity theorem\nof Suslin--Voevodsky, see e.g. [@cd16 Theorem 4.5.2].\n\n::: {#cor:dametassheaves .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *Under the assumptions of\n[1](#lem:aonelocalisationetale){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:aonelocalisationetale\"}, the functor\n$L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!$ induces a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\mathcal{DAM}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* By [1](#lem:aonelocalisationetale){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:aonelocalisationetale\"} $L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!$ is\nfully faithful. Since\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis generated by the objects $R_S^{\\textnormal{tr}}(X)$ for $X$ finite\nétale over $S$ under colimits and finite limits,\n$L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!$ lands in\n$\\mathcal{DAM}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)$. On the other hand,\n$\\mathcal{DAM}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)$ is generated as a\nlocalising subcategory of effective motives by objects in the essential\nimage of $L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!$ and the latter is closed under\ncolimits and finite limits since $L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!$ is a fully\nfaithful exact left adjoint. Hence the claim. ◻\n:::\n\nIn the non-hypercomplete case, recall from\n[1](#lem:inclusionderived){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:inclusionderived\"} that the functor\n$$\\iota_!: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nis fully faithful. Furthermore, its composition with $L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}$\nlands in $\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)$, but we will not be able\nto say that the composition is fully faithful since in this case we have\nno cohomology computations available.\\\nIn the Nisnevich case,\n[1](#rem:alternativeproof){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:alternativeproof\"} asserts that a presheaf with transfers\non finite étale schemes is automatically a sheaf. In the étale case the\nsituation is dual: an étale sheaf on finite étale schemes automatically\nhas transfers. In order to show this, we need a preliminary construction\nthat refines the pullback diagram of\n[1](#defi:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:sheaveswithtransfers\"}.\n\n::: {#cons:refinedpullback .cons}\n**Construction 1**. *The functor\n$\\gamma: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$\nfactors as\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\stackrel{\\rho}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R \\stackrel{\\gamma \\times \\sigma}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\times \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\stackrel{\\times_S}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R).$$\nHere $\\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R$ is the category of finite rank free\n$R$-modules, and by [@lur18 Remark D.1.1.5] we have\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$.\nThe functor $\\rho$ is the identity on the fist factor and constant with\nvalue $R$ on the second, $\\sigma$ is the canonical additive functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ that sends\n$R$ to $S$, and the bifunctor $(-)\\times_S(-)$ comes from the monoidal\nstructure on $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$. We denote the composition\nfunctor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$\nby $\\delta$. Using\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\textnormal{bi-}\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R^\\textnormal{op},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$,\nthe pullback square of\n[1](#defi:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:sheaveswithtransfers\"} refines to the iterated pullback\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:refinedpullback}\n\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R)} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R)} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}^{(\\wedge),\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\delta^*}\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\hat{\\delta}^*}\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}}\", hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\rho^*}\", from=2-1, to=3-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\hat{\\rho}^*}\", from=2-2, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}}\", hook, from=3-1, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=2-1, to=3-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$ As before for $\\gamma$, the presheaf versions of the\nrestriction along $\\rho$ and $\\delta$ are denoted $\\hat{\\rho}^*$ and\n$\\hat{\\delta}^*$, and the sheaf versions $\\rho^*$ and $\\delta^*$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#thm:etaletransfers .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *The functor\n$\\delta^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R)$\nis an equivalence.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We first consider the case of sheaves. Let $S_i$ be the finite\nétale $S$-scheme corresponding to the orbit $G/N_i$, so that the\ncanonical map $G \\to \\textnormal{Aut}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S}(S_i)$\nhas kernel given by $N_i$. Write $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S}$ for\nthe slice $(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S)_{S_i/}$. Then as for $G$-sets\n[@cm21 Construction 4.5] the site $\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ decomposes\ninto a filtered colimit of sites\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S}$ (each of which\nhas covering sieves given by jointly surjective families). The\ntransition maps are the natural maps\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_j}/S}$\nthat precompose with the map $S_i \\to S_j$ whenever there is an\ninclusion $N_i \\subseteq N_j$.\\\nNote that each of the canonical maps\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ is fully\nfaithful. We write $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}({S_i}/S;R)$ for the full\nsubcategory of $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ on the schemes in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S}$. Since each of the maps of sites\ndescends to these correspondence categories (see\n[1](#rem:nicecorrespondences){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:nicecorrespondences\"}), we obtain a similar colimit\ndecomposition\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R) \\simeq \\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}({S_i}/S;R),$$\ncompatible with the functors\n$\\delta_i: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S} \\times \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}({S_i}/S;R)$\nthat are restricted from the functor $\\delta$ of\n[1](#rec:graphfunctors){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rec:graphfunctors\"}. Using the upper pullback of\n[\\[diag:refinedpullback\\]](#diag:refinedpullback){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"diag:refinedpullback\"}, the decomposition of the (pre)sheaf\ncategories involved induces one for sheaves of transfers as a limit\nalong restriction:\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\textnormal{lim}_i \\; \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}({S_i}/S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nSo it suffices to show that each\n$\\delta_i^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}({S_i}/S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{{S_i}/S};R)$\nwhich precomposes with the map $\\delta_i$ from above is an equivalence.\nFor the rest of the proof we will assume that $G$ is finite. The\nargument we give then holds verbatim for each of the $\\delta_i$.\\\nNote that $\\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R$ is the coproduct completion of its\nfull subcategory $\\{R \\} \\subseteq \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R$ on the\nobject $R$, i.e. it is the smallest full subcategory of\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\{R \\})$ that contains the object $R$ and is closed under\nfinite coproducts. Hence [@lur09 Proposition 5.3.6.2] implies that\nrestriction and right Kan extension provide an equivalence\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:latr}\n\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R^\\textnormal{op},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}(\\{R\\}^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).\n\\end{equation}$$ For the moment, we will work with the description on\nthe right-hand side of [\\[eq:latr\\]](#eq:latr){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:latr\"}. Let\n$\\beta: BG \\times \\{R \\} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R \\}$ be\nthe functor that on the first component picks out the scheme $\\tilde{S}$\ncorresponding to the orbit $G/1$ and is given by the identity on the\nother component. Write\n$\\alpha: BG \\times \\{R \\} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ for its\ncomposition with the functor\n$\\delta: \\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_{S} \\times \\{R\\} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$.\nRestriction and right Kan extension along $\\alpha$ provide an adjunction\n$$(\\hat{\\alpha}^*,\\hat{\\alpha}_*): \\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\mathcal{P}(BG \\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nwhich factors as the composition of adjunctions $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}(BG \\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[\"{(\\hat{\\delta}^*,\\hat{\\delta}_*)}\", shift left, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[shift left, from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{(\\hat{\\beta}^*,\\hat{\\beta}_*)}\", shift left, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift left, from=1-3, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ By [@cm21 Example 4.4] (which we already used in\n[1](#lem:sheavesfunbg){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:sheavesfunbg\"}, up to self-duality of $BG$), the functor\n$\\hat{\\beta}_*$ is fully faithful and has essential image those additive\npresheaves that are étale sheaves on the first component (i.e.,\npresheaves corresponding to elements in\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R) \\subseteq \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R)$\nunder the equivalence [\\[eq:latr\\]](#eq:latr){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:latr\"}). We denote the resulting equivalence functor by\n$$\\beta_*: \\mathcal{P}(BG \\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nThe functor $\\alpha$ sends the unique object $(\\ast_{BG},R)$ of its\ndomain to $\\tilde{S}$. By\n[1](#rem:nicecorrespondences){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:nicecorrespondences\"} the endomorphisms of these two\nobjects are isomorphic to the free module $R(G)$, and $\\alpha$ sends a\nmorphism $(g,r)$ to\n$r \\cdot \\langle \\Gamma_{{\\textnormal{id}}^g}\\rangle$, where\n${\\textnormal{id}}^g: \\tilde{S} \\to \\tilde{S}$ corresponds to\nconjugation by $g$. Under the description given in\n[1](#rem:nicecorrespondences){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:nicecorrespondences\"} this corresponds to the element\n$r\\cdot g$ of $R(G)$ and it follows that $\\alpha$ is fully faithful.\nHence the right Kan extension functor $\\hat{\\alpha}_*$ is fully faithful\nas well.\\\nWe now show that $\\hat{\\alpha}_*$ lands in sheaves with transfers. Let\n$\\mathcal{F}: BG^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op}\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$\nbe a functor. For a subgroup $H \\leq G$, the evaluation of the right Kan\nextension $(\\hat{\\alpha}_*\\mathcal{F})(\\tilde{S}/H)$ is computed as the\nlimit of the restriction of $\\mathcal{F}$ to\n$$\\mathcal{Q}\\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=(BG^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op}) \\times_{\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)^\\textnormal{op}} (\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)^\\textnormal{op})_{(\\tilde{S}/H)\\textnormal{\\big /}}.$$\nNow, the functor $\\delta$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-modules\n$$\\textnormal{Hom}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\textsf{\\textup{Lat}}_R}((\\tilde{S},R),(\\tilde{S}/H,R)) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Cor}}_S(\\tilde{S},\\tilde{S}/H)\\otimes R,$$\nhere both sides are isomorphic to $R(G/H)$. It follows that $\\delta$\ninduces an equivalence of $\\mathcal{Q}$ to the diagram\n$$(BG^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op}) \\times_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op}} (\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op})_{(\\tilde{S}/H,R)\\textnormal{\\big /}},$$\nwhich computes\n$\\beta_*\\mathcal{F}(\\tilde{S}/H) \\simeq \\mathcal{F}(\\ast_{BG},R)^{hH}$\n(see also the proof of [@kerodon Proposition 7.3.1.16]). So we have\n$\\hat{\\delta}^*\\hat{\\alpha}_*(\\mathcal{F}) \\simeq \\hat{\\beta}_*(\\mathcal{F})$\nand $\\hat{\\delta}^*\\hat{\\alpha}_*(\\mathcal{F})$ is right Kan extended\nfrom $BG^\\textnormal{op}\\times \\{R\\}^\\textnormal{op}$, and thus a sheaf\nand in particular product preserving. Hence\n$\\hat{\\alpha}_*(\\mathcal{F})$ is a sheaf with transfers. We denote the\nresulting adjunction by\n$$(\\alpha^*,\\alpha_*): \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}(BG \\times \\{R \\}^\\textnormal{op},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nNow, for\n$\\mathcal{G}\\in \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nthere exists\n$\\mathcal{F}\\in \\mathcal{P}(BG \\times \\{R \\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ such\nthat $\\beta_*(\\mathcal{F}) \\simeq \\mathcal{G}$. Since right Kan\nextensions compose we have\n$\\hat{\\delta}_*(\\mathcal{G}) \\simeq \\hat{\\delta}_*\\beta_*(\\mathcal{F}) \\simeq \\alpha_*(\\mathcal{F})$\nwhich is a sheaf with transfers. Hence $\\hat{\\delta}_*$ sends sheaves to\nsheaves with transfers and we denote the resulting functor by\n$$\\delta_*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R\\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nit is right adjoint to restriction along $\\delta$. Now, since $\\alpha_*$\nand $\\beta_*$ are fully faithful, $\\delta_*$ is fully faithful as well.\nSince $\\delta$ is essentially surjective $\\hat{\\delta}^*$ is\nconservative, so since\n$\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}$ is fully\nfaithful $\\delta^*$ is conservative as well. We now have an adjunction\n$\\delta^* \\dashv \\delta_*$ for which the right adjoint is fully faithful\nand the left adjoint is conservative, so this adjunction is an\nequivalence. Since\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\times \\{R\\};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R),$$\nthis finishes the argument for sheaves. The statement for hypersheaves\nfollows from the one for sheaves since the hypersheaf version\n$$\\delta^*: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R)$$\nis the pullback of the functor on sheaves, as in\n[1](#rem:tstructuresheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:tstructuresheaveswithtransfers\"}. Hence it is an\nequivalence as well, which concludes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *In the hypercomplete case, the statement of the previous\nproposition is also implied by [@cd16 Corollary 2.1.9], which relies on\na concrete identification of the effect of the graph functor on\n'representable' sheaves and sheaves with transfers. We also refer to\n[@cm21 Corollary 4.39] for some form of converse for sheaves on the\nsmall étale site, and to [@bh21 Corollary C.13] for a similar statement\nusing $\\infty$-categories of spans.\\\nMorally speaking, étale sheaves on finite $G$-sets already have\ntransfers because they are right Kan extended from $BG$ (at least when\n$G$ is finite) and thus have an overlying Borel complete $G$-spectrum.\\\nOne can make this line of thoughts precise by explicitly identifying the\ncorrespondence category $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ with\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G;R)$, using that by [@fuh25 Corollary 3.17]\nspectral presheaves on the latter are the same as modules over the\nconstant $R$-linear Mackey functor $\\underline{R}$ in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$, and then using that the Borel complete\nsubcategory only sees the restriction of $\\underline{R}$ to the trivial\ngroup.*\n:::\n\nIn the following theorem, we will write\n$\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(G;R)$ for the derived\n$\\infty$-category of $(G;R)$-permutation modules [@bg22a], [@bg23 §3],\n[@fuh25 §4]. It combines the results of the previous sections.\n\n::: {#thm:bigdiagram .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *There is a commutative diagram in which horizontal\nfunctors are equivalences and vertical functors are localisations.\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(G;R)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}  \\\\\n    {\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}  \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).} \n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\alpha\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\beta\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}\", from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"L^h\", from=2-1, to=3-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-2, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"L^h\", from=2-2, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"(-)^{\\wedge}_\\textnormal{ét}\", from=2-3, to=3-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=3-1, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=3-2, to=3-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ If the virtual cohomological dimension of the group $G$\nis finite, all vertical functors from the second to the third row are\nequivalences.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* The content of the statement for the lower two rows was\ndiscussed already: The commutativity of the two bottom squares was shown\nin [1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"},\n[1](#prop:sheavesgrmodules){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesgrmodules\"} and\n[1](#thm:etaletransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:etaletransfers\"}. The assertion about the virtual\ncohomological dimension of $G$ is\n[1](#prop:smashinghypercompletion){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:smashinghypercompletion\"} and\n[1](#cor:smashinghypercompletionreps){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:smashinghypercompletionreps\"}. Let us consider the upper\npart of the diagram.\\\nThe equivalences in the top row hold by [@fuh25 Corollary 4.8, Corollary\n3.18], [@bcn25 Example 2.15] and\n[1](#thm:damnisasmodunderlr){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:damnisasmodunderlr\"} - using that Nisnevich covers in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S$ split the left adjoint in the latter theorem\nfactors through\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$,\nhence is fully faithful, and it clearly hits generators. These\nequivalences are compatible with the filtered colimit decompositions of\nthe three $\\infty$-categories involved we will use below.\\\nBy passing to Ind-objects, [@bg25b Proposition 2.4] implies that the\n$\\infty$-category $\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(G;R)$ decomposes as\na filtered colimit in $\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}$ along\ninflation. Similarly,\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$ by\ndefinition is a $\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}$-colimit along\ninflation. The functor $\\alpha$ for a finite quotient $G_i$ is given as\nthe Ind-extension of the functor\n$$\\mathcal{K}_{\\textnormal{b}}(\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G_i;R)^\\natural) \\to \\mathcal{D}_{\\textnormal{b}}(\\textsf{\\textup{mod}}(G_i;R)) \\to \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$$\nthat is induced by the inclusion\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G_i;R)^\\natural \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{mod}}(G_i;R)$,\nwhere the latter category denotes finitely generated $(G_i;R)$-modules.\\\nUsing (the profinite extension of) [@gs14 §5.2], there is a ring map\n$R_G \\to \\underline{R}$ which is determined by being the unit map\n$\\mathbb{A}_R \\to \\underline{R}$ in $R$-linear Mackey functors on\n$\\pi_0$. The levelwise completion functor of\n[3](#sec:borelprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"sec:borelprofinite\"} induces a functor $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\beta: \\, \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{L_{\\textnormal{lw}(\\underline{R})}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}),}\n    \\arrow[\"{L_{\\textnormal{lw}}}\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ on module categories, where the first equivalence is\n[@lur17 Corollary 3.4.1.9]. By [@fuh25 Construction 3.8, p.39], we can\nwrite $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ as\na $\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}$-colimit along the functors\ninduced by inflation on module categories, followed by an extension of\nscalars along a ring map\n$\\textnormal{infl}_{G_j}^{G_i}(\\underline{R})\\to \\underline{R}$ that is\ndetermined by being the identity on the sections for the trivial group\non $\\pi_0$. Under this description, the functor $\\beta$ identifies with\nthe one induced on colimits by the functors\n$$\\beta_i: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{L_{G_i;R_{G_i}}(\\underline{R})}\\left(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})_{\\textnormal{Borel}}\\right).$$\nEach $\\beta_i$ is the functor induced by\n$L_{G_i;R_{G_i}}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\non $\\underline{R}$-modules. But since the map\n$R_{G_i} \\to \\underline{R}$ becomes an equivalence when restricting to\nthe trivial group, $L_{G_i;R_{G_i}}(\\underline{R})$ identifies with the\nunit of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_{G_i}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G_i})_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$,\nand $\\beta$ lands in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$.\\\nThe functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nis the restriction of the étale sheafification functor to Nisnevich\nsheaves with transfers (which by\n[1](#rem:alternativeproof){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:alternativeproof\"} are just presheaves with transfers),\nsee [1](#rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback\"}.\\\nWe now show that the two upper squares commute. Using the compatibility\nof the above functors with colimit decompositions, it suffices to check\ncommutativity for each finite quotient $G/N_i=G_i$. By the universal\nproperty of the $\\infty$-category in the upper row [@fuh25 Corollary\n3.17] it suffices to establish commutativity of the restrictions to\n$\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G_i;R)$. The latter is the coproduct completion\nof its full subcategory on the permutation modules $R(G_i/H)$ for\n$H\\leq G$, and we can furthermore restrict to this subcategory. In this\ncase, there is a commutative diagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\{R(G_i/H) \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}} & {\\{\\underline{R} \\otimes \\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G_i/H \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}} & {\\{R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(\\tilde{S}_i/H) \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}} \\\\\n    {\\{R(G_i/H) \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}} & {\\{R[G/H_i] \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}} & {\\{R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(\\tilde{S}_i/H) \\mid H \\leq G_i\\}}\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\alpha\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\beta\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-2, to=2-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ in which every node indicates the full subcategory of the\nrespective node in the upper two rows of the diagram in the statement.\nThe centre of the bottom row we view as a full subcategory of\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG_i,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$,\nand under this description the functor $\\beta$ evaluates a spectral\npresheaf on $\\textsf{\\textup{perm}}(G_i;R)$ on $R(G_i)$. For the two\ncategories on the right, $\\tilde{S}_i$ is an $S$-scheme corresponding to\nthe $G$-orbit $G/N_i$, i.e. the kernel of the canonical homomorphism\n$\\varphi: G \\to \\textnormal{Aut}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S}(\\tilde{S}_i)$\nis $N_i$. Note that by\n[1](#rem:representables){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:representables\"} the elements\n$R^{\\textnormal{tr}}_S(\\tilde{S}_i/H)$ are already étale sheaves with\ntransfers. For the behaviour of the bottom right horizontal functor we\nrefer to the proof of\n[1](#thm:etaletransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:etaletransfers\"} - its inverse evaluates on\n$\\tilde{S}_i$. This concludes the proof. ◻\n:::\n\nWe can now amend the diagram of the previous theorem to the right.\n\n::: {#thm:bigdiagramright .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *There is a commutative diagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)} & {\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff}}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(S;R)} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)} & {\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)}\\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{DAM}^{\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R)} & {\\mathcal{DM}^{\\textnormal{eff},\\wedge}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(S;R).}\n    \\arrow[\"{L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!}\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\"', draw=none, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}}\", from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"{L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!}\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"(\\ast)\"', draw=none, from=3-1, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{(-)^\\wedge_\\textnormal{ét}}\", from=2-1, to=3-1]\n    \\arrow[\"(\\ast\\ast)\"', draw=none, from=2-1, to=3-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{(-)^\\wedge_\\textnormal{ét}}\", from=2-2, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"(\\ast\\ast)\"', draw=none, from=2-2, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{(-)^\\wedge_\\textnormal{ét}}\", from=2-3, to=3-3]\n    \\arrow[\"{L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\iota_!}\", from=3-1, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=2-2, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=3-2, to=3-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ in which the top left horizontal arrow is an equivalence.\nWe furthermore have the following implications:*\n\n1.  *If the ring $R$ has positive characteristic $n$ and the residue\n    characteristics of $S$ are prime to $n$, the functor labelled\n    $(\\ast)$ is an equivalence.*\n\n2.  *If the virtual cohomological dimension of $G$ is finite, then the\n    two functors labelled $(\\ast\\ast)$ are equivalences.*\n\n3.  *If $R$ is a $\\mathbb{Q}$-algebra, all vertical functors and hence\n    the horizontal functors on the left side of the diagram are\n    equivalences.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* The functors on Artin motives and effective motives are induced\nby étale sheafification and hypercompletion on smooth $S$-schemes, we\ndenote them by the same symbols as on sheaves with transfers.\nCommutativity of the diagram is clear by construction. The fact that the\ntop horizontal map is an equivalence follows from\n[1](#thm:damnisasmodunderlr){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:damnisasmodunderlr\"}, see also the proof of\n[1](#thm:bigdiagram){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:bigdiagram\"}. Assertion (1) was shown in\n[1](#cor:dametassheaves){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:dametassheaves\"}, (2) was recorded in\n[1](#thm:bigdiagram){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:bigdiagram\"} using\n[1](#prop:smashinghypercompletion){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:smashinghypercompletion\"} and\n[1](#cor:smashinghypercompletionreps){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:smashinghypercompletionreps\"}, and (3) is implied by\n[@cd16 Proposition 2.2.10]. ◻\n:::",
        "heading": "Smooth Artin motives"
      },
      {
        "body_markdown": "Using the language of triangulated categories, (effective) Voevodsky\nmotives (for the Nisnevich topology or more generally for other\ntopologies on smooth schemes) are classically defined by deriving the\n$1$-category of Nisnevich sheaves with transfers and then localising\nwith respect to $\\mathbb{A}^1$ [@cd19 §11]. On the other hand,\ndefinitions using $\\infty$-(pre)sheaves are present in the literature\n[@ek20; @bh21]. In this appendix we show that our definition of sheaves\nwith transfers (that is, before $\\mathbb{A}^1$-localisation) agrees with\nthe more classical one that uses derived categories, thereby also\njustifying that we use classical computations of mapping spaces in\neffective motives. For this, we will focus on hypersheaves, which on the\ncategorical level correspond to derived $\\infty$-categories of\n$1$-categorical sheaves. We keep all standing assumptions from the\nprevious section.\\\nWe first recall a few facts about the $\\infty$-category of additive\npresheaves with values in an $\\infty$-category which for our purposes\nwill always be spectra or an $\\infty$-category of modules in spectra.\n\n::: {#rec:psigma .rec}\n**Recollection 1**. *Let $\\mathcal{C}$ be an $\\infty$-category which\nadmits finite coproducts. Let\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C}) \\subseteq \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) = \\textnormal{Fun}(\\mathcal{C}^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}})$\nbe the full subcategory on presheaves that preserve finite products.\nThen $\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$ is compactly generated [@lur09\nProposition 5.5.8.10(6)] and an accessible localisation of\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ [@lur09 Proposition 5.5.8.10(1)], we write\n$$L_{\\Sigma}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$$\nfor the left adjoint localisation functor. The Yoneda embedding\n$y: \\mathcal{C}\\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ factors through\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$ [@lur09 Proposition 5.5.8.10(2)].\\\nLet $\\mathcal{C}$ be additively symmetric monoidal[^12] and let\n$\\mathcal{D}$ be a presentably symmetric monoidal stable\n$\\infty$-category. Then the presheaf $\\infty$-categories\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ and $\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$\nbecome symmetric monoidal under Day convolution [@lur17 §2.2.6, 4.8.1].\nThese structures make the map\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$\ninduced by the unit $\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}\\to \\mathcal{D}$ in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}})$ symmetric\nmonoidal, see [@nik16 Corollary 3.7] or [@bs24 Proposition 3.3].\\\nAs in [@bgs20 Lemma 3.7] the tensor product on\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ preserves $L_{\\Sigma}$-equivalences in both\nvariables since it preserves colimits in each variables, and\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$ by [@lur17 Proposition 2.2.1.9]\ninherits a symmetric monoidal structure from $\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$\nwhich informally is given by performing a Day convolution in\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C})$ and then applying the localisation functor\n$L_{\\Sigma}$. This makes\n$L_{\\Sigma}: \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$\nand $y: \\mathcal{C}\\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C})$\nsymmetric monoidal.\\\nIf $\\mathcal{C}$ carries a Grothendieck topology $\\tau$ such that the\ntensor product on $\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$ preserves\n$a^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}$-equivalences, then tensoring in\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$ followed by (hyper)sheafification\nendows\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\mathcal{C}; \\mathcal{D})$\nwith a symmetric monoidal structure which makes it presentably symmetric\nmonoidal.\\\nAnalogously, the full subcategory\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D}) \\subseteq \\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$\non $\\mathcal{D}$-valued presheaves which preserve finite products is a\nsymmetric monoidal localisation of\n$\\mathcal{P}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$, cf. [@aok20 Remark 2.10]. When\n$\\mathcal{D}= \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ we write\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};R)$. By [@ggn15 Corollary 2.10(iii),\nExample 5.3(ii)] or [@lur18 Proposition C.1.5.7] there is a symmetric\nmonoidal equivalence\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C}) \\simeq \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}_{\\geq 0})$\nwhich is induced by the functor\n$\\Omega^{\\infty}: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}_{\\geq 0} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}$.\nTogether with the inclusion of connective spectra into spectra this\ninduces a symmetric monoidal and fully faithful 'stable Yoneda\nembedding'\n$$\\bar{y}: \\mathcal{C}\\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C}) \\simeq \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}_{\\geq 0}) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nas in [@aok20 Corollary 2.9]. For $\\mathcal{D}$ presentably symmetric\nmonoidal and stable the essentially unique symmetric monoidal left\nadjoint $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}\\to \\mathcal{D}$ again induces a symmetric\nmonoidal functor\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\mathcal{C};\\mathcal{D})$.*\n:::\n\nRecall that [1](#defi:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:sheaveswithtransfers\"} defined (hyper)sheaves with\ntransfers as the pullback $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:pullbacksheaveswithtransfers}\n\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}^{(\\wedge),\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\tau}}\", hook]\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1, \"\\gamma^*\"]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2, \"\\hat{\\gamma}^*\"]\n    \\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}}\", hook]\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$\n\nThe following two remarks are formulated for smooth $S$-schemes, but\nthey hold verbatim after replacing smooth by finite étale schemes. As in\n[5](#sec:motives){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"sec:motives\"},\n$\\tau$ stands for either the Nisnevich or the étale topology.\n\n::: {#rem:pushoutinsteadofpullback .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *By [1](#rec:psigma){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rec:psigma\"} the functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{o}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}: \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nhas a left adjoint (hyper)sheafification functor\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}: \\mathcal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nThe forgetful functor\n$\\hat{\\gamma}^*: \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nhas a left adjoint given by left Kan extension\n$$\\hat{\\gamma}_!: \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nalong $\\gamma: \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S\\to \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$,\nwhich restricts to $\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}$ by [@chll24 Proposition\n3.3.2]. This means that\n[\\[diag:pullbacksheaveswithtransfers\\]](#diag:pullbacksheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"diag:pullbacksheaveswithtransfers\"} is a pullback in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{R}}_{\\textnormal{st}}$, and we denote\nthe left adjoints to $\\gamma^*$ and\n$\\textsf{\\textup{o}}^{(\\wedge),\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\tau}$ by $\\gamma_!$\nand $\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge), \\textnormal{tr}}$\nrespectively. It follows formally that\n$\\gamma_! \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge), \\textnormal{tr}} \\circ \\hat{\\gamma}_!$.\nWe can hence express\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nas the $\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}_{\\textnormal{st}}$-pushout\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).}\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-1, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge), \\textnormal{tr}}}\"']\n    \\arrow[from=2-1, to=1-1, \"\\gamma_!\"']\n    \\arrow[from=2-2, to=1-2, \"\\hat{\\gamma}_!\"']\n    \\arrow[from=2-2, to=2-1, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}}\"']\n    \\arrow[\"\\usebox\\pullback\"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ Furthermore, both functors $\\hat{\\gamma}_!$ and\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}$ admit symmetric monoidal\nenhancements (using [1](#rec:psigma){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rec:psigma\"} and [@bs24 Proposition 3.6]), and since\n$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}$ is a localisation this pushout\ncan also be computed in\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}_{\\textnormal{st}})$.\nThe resulting symmetric monoidal structure on\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nagrees with the one inherited from\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nas a symmetric monoidal localisation, in the sense of [@lur17\nProposition 2.2.1.9].*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:tstrucuresonsheaveswithtransfers .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *The stable $\\infty$-categories defining the pullback\nsquare in [1](#defi:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:sheaveswithtransfers\"} carry t-structures. For\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ and\n$\\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nboth connectivity and coconnectivity are detected levelwise, see e.g.\n[@bcn25 Definition 2.5]. This makes the restriction\n$$\\hat{\\gamma}^*: \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\ninto a t-exact functor. For\n$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nwe already discussed the t-structure in\n[1](#rem:tstructureonsheaves){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:tstructureonsheaves\"}, it makes the (hyper)sheafification\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{a}}^{(\\wedge)}_{\\tau}: \\mathcal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\ninto a t-exact functor. There is an induced t-structure on\n(hyper)sheaves with transfers for which coconnectivity is detected on\nthe level of presheaves with transfers, i.e. levelwise, and the\nconnective objects are determined by orthogonality. The hearts of these\nt-structures are the abelian categories of (pre)sheaves (with transfers)\nwith values in abelian groups.*\n:::\n\nWe will now compare the $\\infty$-category of hypersheaves with transfers\nof [1](#defi:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"defi:sheaveswithtransfers\"} with the derived\n$\\infty$-category of the Grothendieck abelian category of $\\tau$-sheaves\nwith transfers\n$$\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R) \\subseteq \\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R).$$\nNote that in [@cd19 §10] and [@cd16], Cisinski--Déglise use a\ncoefficient ring $\\Lambda$ for the finite correspondences, which is a\nlocalisation of $\\mathbb{Z}$ at the invertible primes of $R$, or\nequivalently the maximal subring $\\Lambda \\subseteq \\mathbb{Q}$ such\nthat $R$ is a $\\Lambda$-algebra. They then work with $\\Lambda$-linear\n(pre)sheaves\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\Lambda)^\\textnormal{op}\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(R)$.\nBut by [@cd19 Remark 9.1.3] we have\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\Lambda) \\cong \\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z}) \\otimes_{\\mathbb{Z}} \\Lambda$,\nand there is an equivalence\n$$\\textnormal{P}_{\\Lambda\\textnormal{-lin}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\Lambda);R) \\simeq \\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R)$$\nwhich descends to sheaves with transfers. We will work with the latter\ncategory.\n\n::: {#thm:derivedsheaveswithtransfers .thm}\n**Theorem 1**. *There is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal\n$\\infty$-categories\n$$\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R)) \\simeq \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\tau}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* By [@cd19 §10] we have a diagram of adjunctions between\nGrothendieck abelian categories in which we use uppercase letters to\ndistinguish the functors from the ones on $\\infty$-categorical\n(pre)sheaves. $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:sheaveswithtransfers}\n\\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=0.9cm,row sep=0.9cm]\n    {\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R)} & {\\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R)} \\\\\n    {\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R)} & {\\textnormal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R),}\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}}\"', shift right=2, hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\Gamma^*}\", shift left=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=2, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}}\"', two heads, shift right=2, from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=3, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\hat{\\Gamma}^*}\", shift left=2, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=4, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\Gamma_!}\", shift left=2, from=2-1, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=5, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}}\"', shift right=2, hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=6, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\hat{\\Gamma}_!}\", shift left=2, from=2-2, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=7, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}}\"', two heads, shift right=2, from=2-2, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=2, to=0]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=4, to=1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=7, to=5]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=6, to=3]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$ By definition of\n$\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R)$ the\ndiagram of right adjoints is a pullback. According to [@cd19 Proposition\n10.3.3, 10.3.9] the functors $\\hat{\\Gamma}^*$ and $\\Gamma^*$ admit a\nfurther right adjoint, in particular they are exact, and the two\nsheafification functors $\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}$ and\n$\\textsf{\\textup{A}}^{\\textnormal{tr}}_{\\tau}$ are exact as well. We\nhence obtain a diagram of adjunctions of derived $\\infty$-categories\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:derivedsheaveswithtransfers}\n\\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=0.9cm,row sep=0.9cm]\n    {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R))} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R))} \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R))} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R)).}\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}}\"', hook, shift right=2, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\Gamma^*}\", shift left=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=2, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}}\"', two heads, shift right=2, from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=3, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\hat{\\Gamma}^*}\", shift left=2, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=4, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textbf{\\textup{L}}\\Gamma_!}\", shift left=2, from=2-1, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=5, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}}\"', hook, shift right=2, from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=6, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textbf{\\textup{L}}\\hat{\\Gamma}_!}\", shift left=2, from=2-2, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=7, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}}\"', two heads, shift right=2, from=2-2, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=2, to=0]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=4, to=1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=7, to=5]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=6, to=3]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$ The right derived functors\n$\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{(\\textnormal{tr})}$ are\nfully faithful by the argument used in the proof of [@ser03 Corollary\n4.1], which boils down to the fact that the derived right adjoints can\nbe computed using a K-injective resolution (which is a fibrant\nreplacement with respect to the injective model structure of [@lur17\nProposition 1.3.5.3]). According to [@lur09 Proposition 5.5.7.6] the\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{R}}$-pullback of the cospan\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:derivedcospan}\n\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R))} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R))} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R))}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\hspace*{-0.16cm}\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}}\", hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"{\\hat{\\Gamma}^*}\"', from=1-3, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$ is computed in\n$\\widehat{\\textsf{\\textup{Cat}}}_{\\infty}$, and hence it is equivalent\nto the full subcategory\n$$\\mathcal{C}\\subseteq \\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}_{\\Sigma}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;\\mathbb{Z});R))$$\non complexes of presheaves with transfers $F_\\bullet$ such that\n$\\hat{\\Gamma}^*(F_\\bullet)$ lies in the essential image of the fully\nfaithful functor\n$\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}: \\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{Sh}_{\\tau}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R)) \\hookrightarrow \\mathcal{D}(\\textnormal{P}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_S;R))$.\nThe latter is equivalent to the unit map $$\\begin{align}\n\\label{eq:unitpullback}\n\\hat{\\Gamma}^*(F_\\bullet) \\to \\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}\\hat{\\Gamma}^*(F_\\bullet)\n\\end{align}$$ being an equivalence. Since the sheafification functors\nand the functors that forget transfers are exact before derivation,\n[@cd19 Proposition 10.3.9] implies that the target of this map\nidentifies with\n$\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}\\Gamma^*\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}(F_\\bullet) \\simeq \\hat{\\Gamma}^*\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}(F_\\bullet)$.\nThe resulting map\n$\\hat{\\Gamma}^*(F_\\bullet) \\to \\hat{\\Gamma}^*\\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}(F_\\bullet)$\nidentifies with $\\hat{\\Gamma}^*$ applied to the unit map $$\\begin{align}\n\\label{eq:unitpullbacki}\nF_\\bullet \\to \\textbf{\\textup{R}}\\textsf{\\textup{O}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}\\textsf{\\textup{A}}_{\\tau}^{\\textnormal{tr}}(F_\\bullet).\n\\end{align}$$ Since $\\hat{\\Gamma}^*$ is faithful and exact on abelian\ncategories, it is conservative on derived categories.
